post.summary: `POST /api/auth/oidc/backchannel-logout` — OIDC Back-Channel Logout 1.0.
post.description:
Keycloak (or any conformant IdP) calls this server-to-server when a user logs
out or their session ends upstream. There is no cookie and no CSRF token on
this request — it's secured entirely by the logout token's JWS signature
(verified against the provider's JWKS, `iss`/`aud`/`exp` enforced) — see
[`crate::oidc::verify_logout_token`]. On success, every egret session for the
token's `sub` is revoked. An unrecognized `sub` (e.g. a user who never
completed OIDC login) is a no-op 200, matching the spec's guidance that the
RP should not leak whether it knows a given subject. Always sets
`Cache-Control: no-store` per the Back-Channel Logout spec.

200.description: Logout token accepted; matching sessions (if any) revoked

400.description: Missing/invalid logout token, or JWKS unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /engines/{id}/catalogs/{cid}/test` — "test connection": runs
`SHOW SCHEMAS FROM "<catalog>"` against the engine's Trino coordinator via
the native-monitor coordinator proxy ([`crate::monitor::coordinator_call`],
same service name + auth headers as query monitoring) and reports whether
the query reaches `FINISHED`. Submits `POST /v1/statement`, then follows
`nextUri` (GET) until a terminal state, an `error` object, or
[`CATALOG_TEST_MAX_POLLS`] iterations are exhausted (→ `ok:false`,
"timed out"). Never returns a transport/coordinator-shape failure as an
HTTP error status — those map to `ok:false` with an explanatory message —
EXCEPT when the coordinator itself is unreachable or kubernetes isn't
configured, which surface as the usual `CpError` (mirrors the other
coordinator-proxied routes in this file and in `monitor.rs`).
post.description:
SP3c-2 Task 4 deleted this route's five siblings but KEPT this one: it is
the only route in the product that tests a *named engine's* view of a
catalog. The registry's `POST /catalogs/{id}/test` (`test_registry_catalog`
in `catalogs.rs`) picks an applied Trino attachment across ALL of a
catalog's engines and cannot be pointed at one, and it gates on
`catalog_registry:read`, and it tests an applied attachment across ALL of a
catalog's engines rather than one named engine. This route is the only
ENGINE-SCOPED test, which is why it survived SP3c-2 Task 4 while its five
siblings did not.

It is NOT kept for an `engine:read`-only persona, whatever an earlier draft
of this comment said. Task 3 re-pointed `EngineDetail.tsx`'s Catalogs tab at
the registry list, so that operator now sees a 403 pane and zero rows —
there is no `cid` for them to press Test on. `EngineDetail.tsx`'s per-row

post.summary:
`POST /engines/{id}/rotate-secrets` — mint a new Trino internal-communication
secret and `egret-monitor` password and re-apply the engine (pods roll). The
new pair is recorded on the row even if the apply fails — the cluster may
already have received it — so a failed rotation's pair is kept resolvable,
never deleted, alongside whatever it superseded. A later successful
rotation deletes only the ONE pair its own apply superseded; anything
further back (left by an earlier failed rotation, or by a losing
concurrent apply) stays orphaned but resolvable until the engine itself is
deleted — a wider sweep here could destroy a pair a DIFFERENT, still
in-flight apply on this engine just minted, which is the one thing this
route must never do.

post.description:
# What this answers with, and why it changed (SP4d-2a)

Until SP4d-2a this handler evaluated egret's OWN permission model
(`egret_perm::eval::evaluate`) and never read `policy.authz_policies` at
all. The engine evaluates the compiled artifact it downloads from egret.
Those were two implementations of one question, and they had already been
measured disagreeing in production — a predecessor package caught `explain`
reporting a decision the engine did not make. So there is now ONE answer
and it is the engine's: the disagreement class disappears instead of
becoming visible.

It also removes a real blindness. Auto-bind seeds thirteen `egret-admin`
hierarchies granting `*` on everything onto every generated profile
(`egret_policy::default_policies`), and the model-only evaluator could not
see one of them: an operator asking "why can this person read that?" got
`no_grant_matched` while the engine allowed.

Four properties of the implementation below are load-bearing:

1. **The artifact is assembled by [`artifact_via`], which mirrors
   `download_policies` field for field and loads each profile's policy set
   through `enabled_policies_for_service` — the same assembler the download
   route uses, not `list_policies`.** "What explain evaluated" and "what the
   engine received" must not be able to drift.
2. **`roles` and `groups` are empty** — see [`ExplainSubject`].
3. **`resolved_tags` carries egret's own resolution, and
   [`resolved_tags_for_target`] is what decides whether it may.** Until
   SP4d-2b Task 7 this was `None` unconditionally, which made every verdict on
   every catalog a profile serves `Undecidable` while that profile's tag block
   held any policy at all. It is now a real tag set for the one resolution
   shown enricher-equivalent, and still `None` — so still a refusal — for
   every state where it is not. The whole argument is on that function.
4. **A `write` explain is several evaluations**, one per Ranger access type
   the action maps to on that engine, reported separately.

200.description: One verdict per profile over the artifact each engine downloads — including the `no_profile_serves_the_catalog` outcome for a catalog that exists and that no profile serves, which is an answer and not an error

400.description: The target skips a resource level (a column implies a table implies a schema), names a level as "" or "*" (Ranger's "every value", not a resource name), or names a catalog id no registered catalog has

403.description: Missing policy:read permission, or a workspace-scoped impersonation overlay asking about a catalog that workspace is not assigned

# SP4d debt Task 16: the tag branch

Until Task 16 this handler had no `is_tag_kind` branch, so a `tag-*` form
reached `editor_to_ranger_json` and came back `"unknown policy kind:
tag-masking"`. `create_policy` had the branch and `delete_policy_handler`

platform_admin) starts impersonating a MEMBER of that workspace. The resulting

Guards run in a deliberate order so a caller learns nothing before its own
authority is proven: (1) not already impersonating; (2) caller is `ws_admin`

non-empty, target exists, and — because the overlay THIS endpoint writes is
workspace-scoped — the target holds NO platform-scoped role grant at all;

which no `/api/control-plane` route confines, and it is deliberately WIDER here
than on the platform endpoint); (4) the target is a
MEMBER of this workspace and is NOT itself a `ws_admin` of it. Step-up re-auth
then mirrors the platform endpoint: a local caller re-enters their password; an
OIDC caller gets a `409` with an authorize URL whose sealed intent carries this
`workspace_id`, and the overlay is created by the OIDC callback.

decodes with `serde_urlencoded`, which answers

that is a **400**, body ``Failed to deserialize query string: duplicate

parameter accepts for more than one value, and a caller who reaches for

answer. `a_repeated_state_key_is_refused_rather_than_silently_narrowed`

An earlier version of this comment claimed the opposite — that a
repeated key is silently reduced to its last value. The DESIGN it
defended was right and the MECHANISM was false, and the mechanism is
what shipped: it reached `openapi.json` and the generated TypeScript
JSDoc, where a frontend author would have read it and reasoned from it.
**A decision and its mechanism are two claims, and the next person
reasons from the mechanism.**

get.summary: An execution's log lines after a cursor, in `id` order.
get.description:
**Lines appear about 2 seconds after they are written (the settle lag,
[`crate::logs::SETTLE_LAG`]).** A page stops before the first line whose
`inserted_at` is less than 2 s old, and serves nothing above it. The reason
is out-of-order commits: `bigserial` ids are allocated at insert and
committed later, so with two writers (two egret replicas) id 100 can
commit after id 101. A client that had read 101 and moved its cursor past
it would never see 100. Holding lines back until the lowest unserved one
has settled lets the lower id commit first, provided a log write lasts less
than half the lag (a log batch is one short `INSERT`).

**When to stop polling: on `complete && items.is_empty()`, never on a
terminal `execution_state` alone.** A run's lines are inserted before its
outcome commits (`RunLog::finish` waits on the log writer's flush barrier),
so once the execution has been terminal for longer than the settle lag,
every line it will ever have is visible; `complete` says exactly that,
computed from the execution row itself. A terminal state seen earlier can
still have its last lines inside the lag. `complete` does NOT mean every
line the run printed was stored: see spec §11 for the cases (the process
dying, a dropped batch, a log-write fault during which the barrier does not
wait, a run executed twice).

Authorisation is exactly `GET …/executions/{id}`'s: `WsContext` (session,
membership, the `workflows` feature gate), then `workflow:read`, then
[`ExecutionRepo::log_status`] for existence and ownership (the same
contract as `ExecutionRepo::get`, one row, no source or task runs) -- **an
execution in another workspace is a 404, never a 403** -- and only then the
page, which filters on the workspace AND the execution again.

post.summary: Run a finished execution again.
post.description:
# It is a start, deliberately, and from the FROZEN source

`worker::start_execution` with `workflow.executions.source` and
`workflow.executions.inputs` — the row's own copies, not a re-read of the
draft. `worker::replay::spawn_due` takes the same decision for the
`CREATE_NEW_EXECUTION` replacement and states the reason: *"a replay that
picked up an edit made since would be a different flow with the same
trace."* Starting from the draft is what `POST .../flows/{id}/executions`
is for, and the two routes exist to be different.

# The link is `replayed_from_execution_id`, not a parent

`replay::spawn_due` links its replacement with `parent_execution_id` set and
`parent_run_ix` NULL. That slot is **one per execution and already spoken
for**: migration 0138's `workflow_executions_loop_run_idx` is
`UNIQUE (parent_execution_id, parent_run_ix, loop_index) NULLS NOT DISTINCT
WHERE parent_execution_id IS NOT NULL`, so `(X, NULL, NULL)` can exist once,
and `spawn_due` reads exactly that to answer "it already exists". A manual
replay that took the slot would make a later retry-replay of the same
execution fail a unique constraint, and a second manual replay fail one too.

So the replacement has no parent, and the link has a column of its own:
`replayed_from_execution_id` (migration 0166, W9a spec §4.4 item 3), written
here through `start_execution_in` in one transaction with the row. It is
what lets a replay read its source's files (a replay copies its source's
inputs verbatim, and those may be `kestra://` URIs of the source). The audit
record still carries both ids.

# Not a loop iteration

An iteration (`parent_execution_id` with a `loop_index`) is refused (400)
naming its loop root: it is a part of the root's run, `replay::spawn_due`
never replays one, and a replay of it would be a top-level run of the
loop's body alone.

# Terminal only

A non-terminal execution is refused (409) rather than replayed: two RUNNING
executions of one flow, a replay and its original, would be in flight at
once, and the narrow door cannot over-accept. `RunState::is_terminal` is the predicate — read through
`worker::from_wire`, which is derived from `RunState::ALL`, so a state added
to the enum is classified here without anyone remembering to come back.

201.description: A NEW execution, started from the replayed one's frozen source and inputs. The body is the new execution, not the old one — read its `id`.

400.description: The execution is a **loop iteration** (replay its loop root instead); or the **flow's current draft** does not parse, so whether it is disabled cannot be decided; or the replayed execution's frozen source no longer plans, or uses a task type this deployment does not serve

post.description:
W7b Task 3 fix round 1, the user's ruling of 2026-10-11, after review
found the old route released nothing a human needs: it only re-settled,
which ends a pause whose deadline had passed -- what the waker does anyway.
It now calls [`worker::resume_by_hand`](crate::worker::resume_by_hand),
Kestra's `ExecutionService.resume`: every paused `Pause` run ends `SUCCESS`
now, through the natural end's own path, and the execution settles on.

The `PAUSED` check is made twice: here off the scoped read (so a foreign id
never reaches the unscoped worker, and the common refusal is cheap), and
again by the worker under the execution's lock, which decides the race with
the waker. A pause the waker ended first is a 409, like any execution that
is not paused.

parameters.description: Pin the request to a published version of this endpoint, so a publish does not move this caller until they choose to move. The number is the `version` in `meta`, and the `x-egret-version` stamped on this operation in the generated per-service-account document. 504.description: `timeout` — the endpoint's statement exceeded the time budget its author published (`limits.timeout`); the fix is the endpoint's, not the caller's. `deadline_exceeded` — the request outran egret's own serving deadline. Two codes for one status on purpose: they name two different actors, and `code` is what tells them apart

AccessPolicyWritten.description:
What a clearance write actually reached — **SP4c review I5.**

The endpoint used to answer a bare `{"ok": true}`, so a clearance authored
on a Trino profile with no usable `tagService`, or one naming only groups,
was reported as saved while the compiler had emitted nothing at all and the
UI showed it as active. `skipped` carries exactly what the perm mutation
responses already carry (`SkipReport`, same schema) and for the stated
reason: an author needs to know at authoring time, not from a query that
later returns rows it should not.

An EMPTY `skipped` is the normal answer and means every profile a clearance
can reach compiled it.

ok.description: Always `true` — the write committed, or this response was never built.

skipped.description: Every profile/item the accompanying recompile could not express.

AccessRequestDto.description: A join request as seen by the requester.

Ack.description:
The uniform acknowledgement body `{ "ok": true }` returned by mutating
endpoints that have nothing else to say (delete, cancel, …).

Action.description:
The two actions SP4a knows. `read` compiles to `select` on every engine;
`write` compiles to `insert,delete` on Trino (no `update` access type
exists there) and `insert,update,delete` on StarRocks. DDL is out of
scope for SP4a — see the programme's global constraints.

request_method.description:
What the caller asked for. The ONLY identification a row carries when
`endpoint_id` is null — see migration 0125.

actor_user_id.description: Non-null ⇒ a Try-it run by this person, not consumer traffic.

ActivityRange.description:
The four ranges the UI offers, and the only ones it may ask for.

A fixed set rather than a date picker: every query here narrows on
`access_log_ws_ts_idx (workspace_id, ts DESC)`, and the presets are what keep
it inside that index's reach. An input that accepts "one year" on the
fastest-growing table in the schema has nothing stopping the person who types
it.

ActivityRow.description:
One line of the statistics table, or — with `endpoint_id: None` — either the
grand total or the unmatched-request bucket, depending on which grouping set
produced it.

p50_ms.description:
`None` when the population is empty — no successful call in range. Zero
would be a measurement; this is the absence of one.

cacheable_calls.description:
The DENOMINATOR for cache-hit rate: successful calls on a version whose
snapshot had caching enabled. Sent raw so the caller can render `—`
rather than `0%` when it is zero — zero of zero is not zero.

retention_days.description:
`DataApiConfig::access_log_retention_days`, passed through so the UI can
disable ranges that reach past it (spec §4.7).

**The UI cannot compute this and must not assume 30 days exist.**
Retention may be shorter, and `0` means keep nothing — the same reading
`AuditConfig::retention_days` has. Without this field someone selects
`30d`, watches the data thin out at the old end, and concludes traffic
fell; the screen would be actively supporting a wrong conclusion.

`None` ⇒ no prune is scheduled (`scheduled_retention` returned `None`),
so nothing is being deleted and every range is honest.

AffectedProfile.description:
One policy profile a write would touch, named so a steward reads
"Trino-prod" rather than a bare id.

AppCapabilities.description:
What the caller may do in this workspace that no single app can answer for.

The per-row `can_write` / `can_manage` say what the caller may do TO an app.
Creating one -- and creating, renaming or deleting an app folder, which
egret-bi's folder routes gate on the same action -- is a workspace question:
an empty list has no row to read it from, and a collaborator holding a write
share on one app has a writable row and still may not create.

can_create.description:
The caller holds `app:write` in the workspace: `POST /apps` will not be
refused for lack of permission.

AppConflict.description:
The 409 body of draft PUT and publish: either the draft moved on
([`AppStaleRevision`], carrying `current_revision`) or the app is in the trash
([`ErrorBody`]). Documentation only — the handlers return one of the two.

database.description:
A database (by name) of this workspace; the template's connection cell
is pre-filled with it.

AppDetail.description: One app, as returned by get / create / update.

can_write.description:
The caller holds `app:write` on THIS app (per object: a share on one app
makes it true on that row only).

can_manage.description: The caller holds `app:manage` on THIS app (sharing, permanent delete).

AppDraft.description: The editable draft. Its revision is also the response `ETag`.

layout.description:
marimo's grid-layout companion file, verbatim JSON; omitted for the default
vertical arrangement.

expected_revision.description: Publish only if the draft is still at this revision (else 409).

source.description: marimo source, at most 1 MiB (1 048 576 bytes).

layout.description: The complete new layout state; omit or send `null` to clear it.

AppSetFolder.description: Move into a folder, or back to Uncategorized with `folder_id: null`.

AppStaleRevision.description: The draft moved on since the caller read it: reload, then retry.

is_owner.description: The caller created this app (metadata only; access is role/share based).

deleted_at.description: Set while the app is in the trash.

can_write.description:
The caller holds `app:write` on THIS app (per object: a share on one app
makes it true on that row only).

can_manage.description: The caller holds `app:manage` on THIS app (sharing, permanent delete).

AppTicket.description:
Where to point the iframe. The URL carries a one-time ticket that expires in
seconds: open it at once, never cache or reload it.

AppTicketRequest.description: Open an app in an iframe on the apps origin.

version_id.description: Run mode only: the version to open. Omitted = the latest published version.

from_revision.description: The draft revision this version was published from; `None` for a restore.

restored_from.description: The version this one republished; `None` for a publish.

ApplyOutcomeDto.description: One engine's result of applying a catalog.

status.description:
`applied` | `failed` | `skipped`. `skipped`: the engine is external, so
egret did not touch it (the attachment is only declared); `error` then
says so.

role.description: Role to grant the requester; defaults to the originally requested role.

expires_at.description: Optional time-boxed expiry for the membership grant.

AssignEngineBody.description: `POST /workspaces/{id}/engines` body: the engine to assign to the workspace.

AttemptDto.description:
One element of [`TaskRunDto::attempts`], as `worker::claim`'s
`attempts_json` writes it.

**The schema of a field that is passed through as stored.** `attempts` is
served as the stored `jsonb` (`serde_json::Value`), and this type is what
the document says it holds; `tests/executions_routes.rs`
(`a_gantt_row_is_computable_from_the_execution_dto_alone`) deserialises a
real run's `attempts` into it, so the two cannot drift silently.

history.description: The attempt's state names, in order, e.g. `["RUNNING","FAILED"]`.

ended_at.description:
Milliseconds after the execution's `created_at`. Absent while the
attempt is open, and on an attempt recorded before migration 0183.

cursor.description: Keyset cursor from a prior page's `nextCursor`.

AuthConfig.description:
Pre-login capability probe returned by `GET /api/auth/config`: tells the
front-end whether the OIDC "Sign in with SSO" button should be shown.

BackfillDto.description:
A `Schedule` trigger's backfill in progress (W7f spec §3.9). Its inputs
and labels are shown to `workflow:read`, as every execution's inputs are.

id.description:
This backfill's id, written on every execution it fires
(`backfill_id`).

current_tick.description: The next window tick to fire.

paused.description: Paused: no window tick fires until it is resumed.

inputs.description: Overlaid on the schedule's `inputs:` key by key.

labels.description: Added to every execution it fires, in this order.

previous_next_evaluation_date.description:
Where the regular schedule resumes when the backfill ends (its
`recoverMissedSchedules` applies from here).

total_ticks.description: The window's ticks, counted at create.

ticks_done.description: The ticks fired (or skipped) so far.

progress.description: 0-100: Kestra's `(current_tick − start) / (end − start)`, rounded, clamped; 100 for an empty span.

type.description:
The type as the source spells it: an Iceberg type for an egret
catalog, the engine's type name otherwise.

BrowseEngine.description: One engine the catalog is attached to.

status.description:
`provisioning`, `running`, `failed` or `deleting`. An external engine's
`running` is a placeholder (migration 0184).

BrowseKind.description: What one level of a catalog holds.

oneOf.description: Where the listing was read; `null` when nothing could be asked.

engines.description: Every engine the catalog is attached to, by name.

items.description:
Schemas, or a schema's tables and views. `null` when `table` is given
or the level was not listed.

columns.description: The table's columns, when `table` is given and it was listed.

oneOf.description: Set exactly when the level could not be listed.
egret's embedded warehouse.
The named engine.

ok.description: Switched, or the backfill paused, resumed or deleted (and committed).

oneOf.description: The trigger's entry after the change, when `ok`.

BulkResultsDto.description: A result per entry, in the order given.

BulkTriggerRef.description: One trigger of a bulk switch.

scope.description:
`Shared` is refused at validate time on a delegated connection: Ranger
filters per principal, so a shared cache would leak across identities.

CannotBackfill.description:
Why the Backfill button is unusable, the first that applies: the flow is
in the trash, the trigger is not a `Schedule`, the caller lacks
`workflow:manage`, the trigger is effective-disabled, its schedule is off
the queue, a backfill already exists.

CardInput.description: Card as supplied by the client when saving a layout.

id.description:
The id this card already has, so a save can UPDATE it instead of replacing it.

Absent means "new card" — which is what every client sent before this field existed, and
what a card the user has just dropped onto the canvas still sends. It is a HINT, not an
instruction: the server keeps the id only when it already belongs to THIS dashboard (see
`replace_layout`), so a stale or borrowed id can never make one dashboard adopt another's
card.

`skip_serializing_if` keeps a body without ids byte-identical to what it was before this
field existed — `update_dashboard_round_trips_through_json_unchanged` caught the `"id":
null` this would otherwise have added to every card of every re-serialized body.

CardRunBody.description:
Optional body for the card-data endpoint: resolved dashboard-parameter filters
to merge into the card chart's persisted query. Reuses `chartquery::Filter`
(the same `{ col, op, value }` shape the chart spec uses), so the frontend
sends exactly what `applyParamsToChart` produces. Each filter's `col` is
validated against the dataset's real columns before it is applied (an unknown
column → 400), and the values/operators are rendered through the same
injection-safe `sql_literal`/`FilterOp` path as the persisted filters.

filters.description: Resolved, dashboard-param-derived filters to AND onto the card's saved query.

temporal_units.description:
Resolved `temporal_unit` dashboard-param overrides: dimension column name ->
temporal unit token (e.g. "month"). Each token is validated against the
`TemporalUnit` enum by `chartquery::build` (an unknown token → 400) and rendered
as an enum-driven bucket expression — never spliced into SQL as a raw string.
A client override replaces the saved unit for that already-gridded column.

CatalogAttachErrorDto.description: One catalog from a create body's `catalogs` that the engine came up without.

message.description: Why the attach failed, in the words the attach route would have used.

CatalogAttachmentDto.description: One engine a catalog is attached to.

applyStatus.description:
`applied` | `failed` | `pending`. `pending` means egret has recorded the
attachment and has not yet been able to tell the engine — a StarRocks
engine whose FE is still coming up (5-10 minutes after create), which
the bootstrap or a Retry converges.

isPrimary.description:
This catalog is that engine's PRIMARY: it leads the engine's render
order and cannot be detached or edited. At most one of an engine's
catalogs carries it (SP3c D2, migration 0150).

createdAt.description:
When this attachment was recorded — `engine_catalog_attachments.created_at`.

The clock a `pending` attachment has been waiting on. `pending` is
written only by the INSERT that creates the row (engine create and
attach; nothing flips a settled attachment back), so this is the moment
the wait began. A UI deciding whether a `pending` has outlived the
StarRocks bootstrap must measure against THIS and not against the
catalog's `updatedAt`: attaching an existing catalog never touches the
catalog row, so its `updatedAt` is already arbitrarily old.

CatalogCheck.description:
Which of the three checks produced a [`CatalogTestResultDto`]. An enum, not
a string, so Task 7's renderer gets a union it must switch on exhaustively:
the whole point of the discriminant is that the three cannot be blurred, and
a doc comment saying "read this first" is a comment doing a type's job (SP3c
review F4). The wire values are unchanged.

CatalogConflictBody.description:
409 body of a refused catalog delete. Two shapes share this struct (same
pattern as `EngineConflictBody`): `code = "catalog_in_use"` carries the
non-empty `engines`/`workspaces` that still use the catalog; `code =
"warehouse_catalog"` (an egret warehouse catalog, refused unconditionally —
delete the warehouse instead) carries neither, so they're omitted.

action.description: `restart` (Trino rolls its pods) | `in_place` (StarRocks rebuilds the connector).

CatalogTestResultDto.description:
`POST /catalogs/{id}/test` payload.

Every field a UI author must read is a schema property, so its doc comment
reaches the generated client as JSDoc — a response description does not.

ok.description:
Whether the check that ran succeeded — and it means only as much as
`check` says it does. Read `check` FIRST: `unsupported` is always
`ok:false` because nothing was measured, and that is not a broken
catalog, so it renders neutral rather than red.

check.description: Which check ran, so a green tick can never be read as the other one.

engineName.description: The engine the query ran on; null for `tcp` and `unsupported`.

target.description:
For `tcp`, the `host:port` that was dialled, so the result names what it
measured; null otherwise.

message.description:
One sentence an operator can act on. For `tcp` it always says, in the
sentence itself, that reachability is all that was measured.

ChangeKind.description:
The stable machine code for one kind of difference between two published
contracts.

A closed enum rather than a free string, and it is what
[`Self::is_breaking`] matches on — so the classification is a single table
that a reader can check against the rule at the top of this module, rather
than a `breaking: true` written by hand at each construction site where one
of them would eventually be wrong.

Serialised in `snake_case` and **recorded in `dataapi.endpoint_versions`**,
so these names are persisted data: renaming one silently reinterprets every
stored row. Add variants; do not rename them.

ChartDataBody.description:
Build-only data request: produce SQL for a dataset + QuerySpec; the client submits it
to the existing /queries endpoint and polls.

Stays in `egret-bi` (not the leaf contract crate): its `query_spec` field is the
`egret-bi`-local [`QuerySpec`] query builder, which references `egret-query-api`
and other in-crate types and so cannot move to the leaf.

ChartRunResponse.description:
A saved chart's query, executed: columns + row-major rows. Mirrors the first
two fields of `TabularResult` so the frontend consumes it like a query
result. Returned by the object-scoped `POST /charts/{id}/data` endpoint,
which runs ONLY the chart's persisted query (no client-supplied spec).

rows.description: Row-major cell values; each inner vec is one row aligned to `columns`.

ClassifiedPolicy.description: One policy of the profile, as the classifier reports it.

enabled.description: The `enabled` COLUMN — what decides whether the engine downloads it.

blockers.description:
Every reason the policy cannot be migrated, as operator-readable
sentences naming the offending value. Empty iff `migratable`.

oneOf.description: For a migratable policy, the model objects it would become.

Present iff `perm.migrated_from` records this policy as migrated —
which is what tells a migrated original apart from one switched off by
hand (both have `enabled = false`). A migrated policy is never
`migratable`, and its one blocker sentence says how to undo it.

warnings.description:
SP4d-4 Task 11: what this policy's resource levels mean to Ranger,
independent of migration — a policy that stops above `column` and
allows `select` grants no column read, and one with a gap decides
nothing. Empty for every row that is neither a hand-written
(`operator`) policy of a resource profile nor affected. **Flagged,
never rewritten**: nothing here edits a stored row.

task_id.description: The flowable's task id; `None` for the triggers cluster.

start.description:
The uid of the cluster's `start` marker node. **Exception: a
`subflow` cluster with a `reason`** (an expansion that could not
happen) has no markers and no nodes; its `start` and `end` are both
the `Subflow` task's own uid, a node that stays in its parent cluster.

end.description:
The uid of the cluster's `end` marker node; for a `subflow` cluster
with a `reason`, the `Subflow` task's own uid (see `start`).

oneOf.description:
Why a `subflow` cluster is empty (spec §3.4): it then has no nodes and
no markers, and `start`/`end` name the `Subflow` task node. `None` on
every other cluster and on a `subflow` cluster that expanded.

ColumnMeta.description: One column's name + engine-reported type name.

ColumnSpec.description:
The frozen form of a `ColumnMeta`. Deliberately its own type rather than
re-using `egret_core::ColumnMeta`: this one is persisted inside a published
snapshot, so it must stay stable even if the engine-facing type gains or
renames a field.

required.description:
Present in EVERY permutation described at publish.

Defaults to `true` when absent, which is what a snapshot written before
this field existed carries. Those columns were checked for equality on
every call, so `true` is the only default that does not loosen an
already-published contract.

CompileResponse.description:
What a mutation's (or `compile`'s) recompile pass did, aggregated over
every service it touched.

ConditionDto.description: One `dependsOn` entry, labelled by its condition key.

met.description: The open window holds this condition as met.

impersonate.description:
Run each query as the logged-in user (impersonate delegation mode).
Trino → `X-Trino-User`; StarRocks → `EXECUTE AS <user> WITH NO REVERT`.
Requires engine impersonation + Ranger. Default false.

tls_cert.description:
PEM of the engine's self-signed cert to pin as a trusted root (server-auth
over TLS). Set on egret-provisioned TLS connections — Trino jwt/TLS mode
(https) and StarRocks delegation (in-band TLS on :9030).

ContractChange.description:
One difference, in the words an author has to act on.

There is deliberately **no `breaking` field**. Which list a change is in IS
its classification ([`ContractDiff`]), so a flag and a kind cannot drift into
disagreeing — the failure mode of every "carry the answer beside the
question" shape this codebase has removed.

subject.description:
What the change is ABOUT: `column `total` of statement `rows``, or
`parameter `region``. Free text for a reader; it is also part of the
acknowledgement digest, so two changes of one kind on two different
subjects cannot be acknowledged by one token.

detail.description:
One sentence naming the old value and the new one. The author is entitled
to know exactly what to fix — a publish-time refusal is an AUTHORING
error, unlike a serving error, where naming the definition would be
context disclosure to a consumer.

ContractDiff.description:
The comparison of a prospective version against the one being served.

Two lists, not one list with a flag: see [`ContractChange`].

breaking.description:
Changes a deployed consumer cannot survive. Non-empty means publish
refuses without an acknowledgement.

safe.description:
Changes that were looked at and judged survivable. Reported rather than
dropped, so "we found nothing" is distinguishable from "we found six
things and none of them matter" — an author who sees the safe list is an
author who can tell that the breaking list being empty means something.

CreateBackfillRequest.description: Create a backfill of a `Schedule` trigger.

start.description:
The window's first instant (inclusive): the first tick at or after it
fires first.

end.description:
The window's last instant (inclusive); absent: the server's now. Must
not be after the server's now.

inputs.description:
Overlaid on the schedule's `inputs:` key by key. An object; no key may
name a `FILE` input.

labels.description:
Added to every execution the backfill fires, in this order. A list of
`{key, value}` or a map.

CreateEndpointInput.description:
The `POST` body.

The spec fields are `Option<T>` rather than `#[serde(default)] T` because
`CacheSpec`/`LimitsSpec`/`RateLimitSpec` deliberately have no `Default` impl —
`OutputSpec`'s hand-written one exists precisely because a derive would have
diverged from serde's defaults. An absent field is stored as `'{}'::jsonb` and
read back through the same serde defaults, so there is exactly one definition
of "the default" and no Rust-side copy of it to drift.
`deny_unknown_fields`: a misspelled TOP-LEVEL key is a 400 naming the field,
not a silently discarded value. Every field here is either required or
`#[serde(default)]`, so nothing legitimate is refused.

This attribute covers only this struct's own keys — it does not reach a
nested one. The nested config types carry their own; see the note above
`ParamSpec` in `egret-dataapi-api`, which is where the reported case
(`{"rate_limit": {"per_client_qps": 5}}` returning 201 with the limit
defaulted to `0`) is actually refused. Both layers are needed.

path.description:
Free-form and user-typed. **Total-reject, not normalised**: a leading
slash is optional and one trailing slash is absorbed, but anything else
out of shape — an empty segment, a `.`/`..` segment, percent-encoding, a
query string, a fragment, whitespace, a character outside
`[A-Za-z0-9._~-]`, or a value over [`MAX_PATH_LEN`] bytes — is a 400
naming the reason. Nothing is silently rewritten. See [`normalize_path`].

database_id.description:
The connection this endpoint queries. Validated against the CALLER's
workspace by the route before it is stored — it arrives from the request
body, so nothing else would stop it naming another workspace's database.

statements.description:
The statements this endpoint runs, in order. Required and non-empty:
[`egret_dataapi_api::validate_statements`] refuses an empty list, a name
that is not an identifier, and a repeated name, all as a 400 naming the
reason — the schema's own `CHECK` behind it means an empty list is not
merely refused here but unrepresentable.

`max_items` puts [`MAX_STATEMENTS`] into the generated contract, which is
the only place a client can learn it: it is a rule
`validate_statements` applies, not a column, so nothing else in the
document said the number at all. utoipa's `max_items` takes a LITERAL, so
it cannot name the constant — the `const _: () = assert!(…)` above this
struct is what stops the two drifting, and it does it at compile time.

warehouseId.description:
Superseded by `catalogs` and dropped in SP3c-2. A body that sends this
and no `catalogs` behaves exactly as it did before; a body that sends
BOTH is refused rather than having one of them quietly ignored.

catalogs.description:
Registry catalogs to attach at create. Exactly one must be `primary`,
and every id must exist — an unknown or repeated id refuses the create
before anything is provisioned. Mutually exclusive with `warehouseId`.
CREATE ONLY: `PUT /engines/{id}` refuses a body that carries it.

trinoConfig.description:
Optional full per-role config surface, stored under `spec["trinoConfig"]`.
Wire shape: `{ queryMaxMemory, logLevel, configProperties, env,
coordinator{replicas, resources, heap, queryMaxMemoryPerNode,
additionalJvmConfig, probes}, worker{... , gracefulShutdown} }`. On create
the simple wizard fields seed this; `update` sends the full per-role block.

authzServiceId.description:
Link the new engine to an EXISTING Ranger profile (authz_services id).
When omitted, provisioning creates a fresh profile named after the engine.

kind.description:
Which engine to provision: `"trino"` (default, back-compat) or
`"starrocks"`. Selects between the Trino spec-building path and
[`create_starrocks_engine`].

oneOf.description:
StarRocks-specific config surface (FE/CN image + replicas + optional
resources); only read when `kind == "starrocks"`. Storage (endpoint/
path/keys) is NOT accepted here — it's derived from the warehouse's
storage connection, same as the Trino S3 connector.

tlsCertSecretRef.description: Optional: a kubernetes.io/tls named secret to back the coordinator TLS.

catalogAttachErrors.description:
Catalogs from the body's `catalogs` that could not be attached. Empty on
success. The engine EXISTS and is provisioned; these catalogs simply are
not on it, and each can be retried with
`POST /api/control-plane/engines/{id}/catalogs/{cid}`. The create is not
rolled back for them — the cluster is already up by the time they are
attached, and the alternative (the wizard's own attach loop) reports a
per-catalog failure exactly the same way. Every id in the body was
resolved BEFORE provisioning, so nothing here is a mistyped id.

CreateEngineResponse.description:
What `POST /engines` returns: the engine, plus whichever of the body's
`catalogs` the engine came up WITHOUT.

Its own type rather than a field on [`EngineDto`] (review F2): `GET`, the
list and `PUT` all return `EngineDto` and can never have anything to say
here, and a schema that advertises a field an endpoint cannot send is a
promise to its consumers that only create keeps. The engine's own fields are
flattened, so the create response is byte-identical to `EngineDto` whenever
`catalogAttachErrors` is empty — which is every create that does what it was
asked.

source.description:
The flow's YAML, byte for byte. `namespace`/`flow_id` are DERIVED from
it (parsed, never accepted as separate body fields) so the stored
identity can never disagree with what the YAML itself declares.

config.description:
Optional service config (e.g. StarRocks JDBC coordinates). Stored verbatim.

A `tagService` key is accepted only when `type` is `"trino"` — see the
handler's doc comment.

name.description: SQL name on every engine: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`, immutable.

kind.description: iceberg | hive | delta_lake | hudi | jdbc | elasticsearch | tpch | tpcds | generic

CreateSchedule.description:
Create body. `type` decides which optional block is required, checked in the
route before the database's CHECK constraints see it, so the client gets a
message naming the missing field rather than a constraint name.

dataapi_endpoint_id.description: `None` is workspace-scoped: watch every endpoint rather than one.

dataapi_error_code.description:
Required, and only meaningful, when `dataapi_metric` is
`error_code_count` — `schedule_dataapi_error_code_needs_metric` /
`schedule_dataapi_metric_needs_error_code` (migration 0128).

message.description:
A user-authored note carried into the notification body. Distinct from
`description`, which is the line the LIST shows.

message_footer.description:
The closing note, rendered UNDER the result — `message` opens the
notification, this one closes it, and an inline image sits between them.
Defaulted, so a client written before 0116 keeps working unchanged.

skip_if_empty.description: Metabase's `skip_if_empty`: send nothing when the run produced no rows.

targets.description:
Objects a REPORT delivers, in page order. Empty falls back to the
single `chart_id`/`dashboard_id`, which is every pre-0115 row.

owners.description:
Owner user ids. Empty means "the creator", resolved server-side — a
schedule with no owner has no identity to run as (§5.2).

CreateSecretInput.description:
Request body for creating a global named secret. Either a typed `data` map
(with `type`, default `Opaque`) or the legacy single `value` (→ Opaque{value}).

value.description: Back-compat: a single value stored as `Opaque{value}`.

CreatedPolicyId.description: Doc-only mirror of the `{ "id": <n> }` body the create/update handlers return.

filledLevels.description:
Present only when this save stored an emptied resource level as `*`
(SP4d-4 Task 11): the level names, root first.

note.description:
Present with `filledLevels`: what the fill means in Ranger — the policy
now covers every child of those levels, and it moved earlier in the
evaluation order of its priority band.

warnings.description:
Present only when the fill moved the saved policy ahead of another
same-band policy that may decide the same request.

CreatedProfile.description: Doc-only mirror of the body `create_profile` returns.

CreatedResponse.description:
A create's response: the id the database minted, and what the recompile
that committed with it did.

created_by_name.description:
Display name for `created_by` — the profile name, else the email. Resolved server-side:
the endpoints that can turn a user id into a name are admin-gated, so the browser cannot
do it for an ordinary workspace editor. Same shape and same reason as
`MemberDto.principal_name`.

created_at.description: NULL for dashboards predating migration 0106, which does not invent a creation date.

updated_by_name.description: Display name for `updated_by`, resolved the same way as `created_by_name`.

folder_id.description:
The folder this dashboard is filed under; NULL = Uncategorized. Present on
`DashboardSummaryDto` since folders shipped, and absent here until now, which is why the
info sidebar had no folder to name.

certified.description:
Marked as trusted by a steward. Same three fields datasets and metrics have carried since
0098, so "is this certified" is one question across the product rather than three.

certified_by.description:
Who certified it, as their email — the string is read by whoever sees the badge, and a
uuid would tell them nothing. Empty while `certified` is false.

certification_details.description:
Why, in the certifier's words. Empty is allowed: a certification with no note is still a
certification.

can_manage.description:
May the CALLER edit this dashboard? Workspace-scoped `dashboard:manage`, answered by the
PDP — the session's permission list carries platform grants only and can never contain it.

DashboardRevisionDto.description:
One entry in a dashboard's History tab.

The `snapshot` is deliberately NOT on this DTO. A 22-card dashboard's PUT body is hundreds of
kilobytes and the cap is twenty of them, so shipping the content would make opening the info
sidebar a multi-megabyte download for a list the user reads as six lines of text. Revert takes
a revision id and does the work server-side, where the snapshot already is.

created_by_name.description:
Display name for `created_by`, resolved server-side for the same reason
`DashboardDetailDto.created_by_name` is.

is_current.description:
True for the revision that matches the dashboard's live state — the newest one. The client
suppresses the revert action on it rather than deriving "newest" from the array order,
which would silently become wrong the day the endpoint gains a sort parameter.

certified.description:
A steward has vouched for this dashboard. Display only — the list carries no
`certified_by`, since the badge here answers "is it trusted", and "by whom" is a
question the detail page already answers.

can_manage.description:
Whether this caller may run the list's mutating actions — duplicate, move, trash,
delete.

WORKSPACE-SCOPED, AND THE SAME ON EVERY ROW. Unlike `DashboardDetailDto.can_manage`,
which is evaluated against the individual object, this is one workspace-level decision
copied across the response. That is deliberate: a per-object answer costs two SQL
queries PER ROW (`grants_for` plus the classification-tag lookup inside `CedarPdp`),
so a 100-dashboard list would issue 200 extra queries to draw a menu.

The cost of the shortcut is a FALSE NEGATIVE, never a false positive: someone who holds
manage only through a per-object or per-folder share sees the row menu withheld here.
They lose nothing they cannot recover — opening the dashboard runs the real per-object
check and gives them the editor. The opposite error, offering Trash to a reader, is the
one that costs.

DataApiClientDto.description:
What a client list returns. There is deliberately NO secret field — not a
skipped one, not an `Option`. A field that cannot exist cannot leak through a
future serde attribute change.

Named with the `DataApi` prefix because utoipa keys components by Rust type
name and those names are GLOBAL after `openapi_doc()` merges the seams —
`egret-catalog-engine` already publishes a `ClientDto`, and a collision
silently overwrites one of them in the merged document.

DataApiEndpointDto.description:
An endpoint draft as the management UI sees it.

Named with the `DataApi` prefix for the same reason `DataApiClientDto` is:
utoipa keys components by Rust type name and those names are GLOBAL once
`openapi_doc()` merges the seams, so a bare `EndpointDto` is a collision
waiting for the next seam that wants the word.

statements.description:
The endpoint's statements, in execution order.

A LIST, not a string, and a one-statement endpoint is the same shape as
a ten-statement one — there is no "simple" spelling to keep in step with
the general one. Stored as `jsonb`, like every other structured column
on this row.

live_version_id.description:
The version currently served. Never written by this module — publishing
is a separate lifecycle.

deleted_at.description:
When this endpoint was moved to the trash, or `null` if it is live in the
authoring sense — present, listed, editable.

On the DTO rather than a bare `trashed: bool` because WHEN it was trashed
is what a "Trash" screen sorts and ages by, and because the column itself
is the timestamp — a boolean projection here would be a second
representation of the same fact for the frontend to disagree with. The
schema's `CHECK (deleted_at IS NULL OR state <> 'live')` (migration 0126)
means a non-null value here can never coexist with `state = "live"`.

DataApiEndpointGrantDto.description: One service account's invoke grant on an endpoint.

service_account_name.description:
The account's display name, so the list is readable without a second
call. `None` if the account row has since been deleted.

bookmarked.description: Whether the CALLER has starred this endpoint. Per user, never global.

DataApiEndpointListItemDto.description:
One row of the endpoint LIST: the draft, plus the calling user's own
`bookmarked` flag.

A separate type rather than a field on [`DataApiEndpointDto`] because that
DTO is also what `GET /endpoints/{id}`, `POST /endpoints`, `PATCH
/endpoints/{id}`, disable/enable and the publish lifecycle's locked read
return — and half of those have no user to be per-user ABOUT. A
`bookmarked` on the create response would be a field that is always `false`
by construction, and one on the lifecycle's read would be a field with
nobody to answer for; either is a value a client could believe. The flag
exists where it is asked for and nowhere else.

`#[serde(flatten)]` so the wire shape stays FLAT — `{...endpoint,
"bookmarked": true}`, one object, exactly as if the field lived on the DTO —
and so a field added to [`DataApiEndpointDto`] tomorrow appears in the list
with nothing here to update. The same idiom `EngineDetailDto` uses; utoipa
renders it as an `allOf`.

DataApiEndpointVersionDto.description: A published version, as the API reports it.

is_live.description: True for the version `endpoints.live_version_id` points at.

snapshot.description:
The frozen definition. **This is the only thing P4 may read to decide what
a request returns** — see the module comment.

breaking_changes.description:
What publishing this version did to the consumers of the one it replaced
(package 6), and therefore what its `created_by` accepted when they
acknowledged it.

`None` and `Some([])` are different facts and are kept apart. `None` is a
version published before this was recorded, or the FIRST version of an
endpoint, where there was no live contract to break. `Some([])` is a
version that was compared against the live one and broke nothing. A
history that showed both as "no breaking changes" would be claiming
something about the first that nobody ever checked.

compared_against_version.description:
The version NUMBER [`Self::breaking_changes`] was compared against —
whatever was live when this one was published.

`None` exactly when `breaking_changes` is `None`. Usually the preceding
version, and after a rollback NOT: `rollback` moves the live pointer
backwards and adds no row, so `Some([])` beside a baseline two versions
down is a comparison that happened and a set of consumers it says nothing
about. The number rather than the id, because this is what a history
renders and a number is what a reader can place.

DataApiNewClientDto.description: The issue response, and the only type in the crate carrying secret material.

token_endpoint.description: Where to exchange these for a token.

DataApiPreviewDto.description:
What a preview answers with.

`columns` carries the ENGINE's own names — `output.naming` is deliberately not
applied, because an author debugging SQL needs the names they wrote, and the
published contract (naming transform included) is what `Response` is for. The
UI must say which is which.

truncated.description:
True when the result was longer than [`PREVIEW_MAX_ROWS`] and this is a
prefix of it. The connector fetches `cap + 1` and sets this rather than
truncating silently, so `row_count == 100` alone cannot tell "exactly at"
from "over".

transform_declared.description:
True when the draft declares an `output.transform` — so `columns` and
`rows` above are the STATEMENT's, and a consumer receives something else
entirely (the script's output, described by `returns`).

A fact, not a rendering: the UI owns the sentence, the way it does for
`truncated`. But it must say something, because this is the one case
where the gap between "what preview shows" and "what a consumer gets" is
not a renaming — it is a different value of a different shape. See the
module comment for why preview does not run the script, and for what
does.

generated_sql.description:
The template the statement's `build_sql` script returned — `{{ }}`
intact, before any render — or `None` when the author wrote the SQL
themselves (package S Task 7).

**Showing it is the point of previewing a script at all.** A script that
branches emits a different statement per parameter value, and until this
field the only way an author could see which one their draft produced was
to publish it and read the engine's error. C2's response transform could
not be previewed and this route says so (`transform_declared`); here the
artefact exists, so it is on screen.

# It is the TEMPLATE, not what the engine ran

The rendered form has the author's values replaced by bind markers, which
is the one thing they cannot edit and did not write. The template is what
they would have typed by hand, so it is directly comparable with the
editor beside it — and it is the artefact the script is responsible for.

# It is generated from the author's own test `values`

Not from publish's representative ones. A preview that showed the
baseline branch while binding the author's values would show a statement
their values do not take — the "told fine, then told no" defect this
route exists to invert, in its quietest form.

# `None`, not an echo, for a written statement

The author is looking at that text in the editor. A field that always
carried something would give the UI no way to tell "this is what your
script built" from "this is what you typed".

DataApiPublishedDto.description: What `publish`/`rollback` report back about the version now being served.

breaking_changes.description:
The breaking changes this publish made, which the caller acknowledged to
get here (package 6).

Echoed back rather than merely stored so the audit event the route emits
carries the same list the version row does — one write, two records, and
no second computation of what was accepted.

`None` for a first publish and for a `rollback`, neither of which
compares anything: a rollback re-serves a contract that was already
published once, and the two live rules it DOES re-ask are the ones whose
inputs are live (see [`EndpointStore::rollback`]).

`skip_serializing_if` here and deliberately NOT on
[`DataApiEndpointVersionDto::breaking_changes`], which is the same value
read back out of the table. There, `null` is an answer — "nobody looked"
— and a reader has to be able to tell it from `[]`. Here the field is
absent from a `rollback`'s response because that response is not about a
comparison at all, and a `null` would invite the reader to interpret it.

compared_against.description:
The version [`Self::breaking_changes`] is a statement ABOUT: whatever was
live at the instant of the publish.

Echoed for the same reason it is stored — see migration `0131`. After a
rollback this is not the version before this one, and an empty list read
without it says more than it knows. `None` for a first publish, and for a
`rollback`, which compares against the version it moved OFF and reports
that under [`Self::rollback_breaks`].

rollback_breaks.description:
What a `rollback` did to the consumers of the version it moved OFF,
classified by the same [`crate::contract::compare_contracts`]
`publish` uses — and refusing nothing.

A separate field from [`Self::breaking_changes`] because it answers a
separate question. That one is read back out of
`endpoint_versions.breaking_changes` and is a record of what an author
ACCEPTED; this one is stored on no row, because a rollback creates no
version. Sharing a field would let a history renderer show a rollback's
consequences as an acknowledgement nobody gave.

`None` for a `publish`, for a rollback onto an endpoint with nothing
live, and when either snapshot cannot be read — a rollback must not fail
because the sentence it was going to say could not be built.

DataApiServiceAccountDto.description:
A service account as the management UI sees it. `id` is the `users.id` — a
service account is a real user row, so this is the id that appears in
`access_grants`, Cedar and audit.

email.description: The synthetic address `users.email` requires. Not a mailbox.

statements.description:
Exactly what `publish` would freeze: one entry per statement, in the
author's order, each carrying the output schema `describe` resolved for
it — so an author sees the contract before committing to it.

A LIST rather than the single `columns` this carried before M2, because
an endpoint has one column set per statement and folding them into one
would report a contract no version will ever hold: two statements each
returning a `total` are two result sets, not one column declared twice.
[`egret_dataapi_api::StatementSnapshot`] rather than a new pair type,
because it IS the frozen shape and reusing it keeps "what validate says"
and "what publish writes" the same words.

oneOf.description:
What publishing this draft would do to the consumers of the version
currently live (package 6).

`null` for an endpoint that has never been published — the FIRST publish,
where no consumer has ever received anything and there is nothing to
break. That is a different fact from an empty diff, which means the two
contracts were compared and found compatible, and the two are kept apart
here for the same reason they are kept apart in the column that records
them.

acknowledge_breaking.description:
The value to send back as `acknowledge_breaking` on `POST …/publish`,
present exactly when `against_live.breaking` is non-empty.

A digest of those breaking changes, not a constant — see
[`PublishEndpointInput::acknowledge_breaking`].

DataapiMetric.description:
The Data API metric a `dataapi_alert` watches — the closed vocabulary of
migration 0128's `schedule_dataapi_metric_valid` CHECK.

A typed enum here, unlike the raw `&str` `egret-automation::dataapi_metric`
matches on internally: an unknown metric then fails to DESERIALIZE — a 4xx
the JSON layer names before `to_new`'s validation ever runs — rather than
reaching Rust as an unchecked string.

Database.description:
A full database registration row (no secret material).

`Serialize`/`Deserialize` are forward-looking contract surface: today the
wire type is the separate `DatabaseDetailDto` and the store builds `Database`
field-by-field from sqlx rows, so these codecs are not yet exercised — they
let a future out-of-process query-seam client exchange this domain type.

delegated.description: B3a: run BI queries as the caller's per-user engine JWT (delegation).

governed.description:
The data behind this connection is governed at the ENGINE — Ranger row
filters and column masks apply to it.

Consumed by `egret-dataapi`, which refuses to publish an endpoint onto a
governed connection unless [`Database::delegated`] or
`options.impersonate` makes the engine run each query as the CALLER. On a
shared service credential those filters are evaluated for the machine
identity, so every consumer of the endpoint reads what the service
account may read.

`#[serde(default)]` for rows and payloads written before the column
existed: `false` is what migration 0130 gave every existing row, and it
is the value that changes nothing. It is NOT the fail-safe direction and
is not claimed to be — the gate is opt-in per database by design (see the
migration's own comment for why the alternative was a migration-time
outage).

engine_id.description:
Set when this row was materialized by an engine→workspace assignment.
A non-null `engine_id` marks the connection provisioned (read-only,
per-user-delegated) and links it back to the source engine.

governed.description:
See [`Database::governed`]. Surfaced on the detail DTO so the Data API
author's database picker can warn BEFORE publish that the connection it
is pointed at cannot carry a governed endpoint.

engine_id.description:
Set (as a UUID string) when this connection was materialized by an
engine→workspace assignment (read-only, provisioned by egret); `None`
for a self-service connection. The frontend uses it to split the
workspace Engines page into provisioned vs. self-service groups.

DatabaseInput.description:
Register/update body. Credentials are a NAMED secret (Epic B): either
`new_secret` (mint a new named secret inline) or `secret_id` (reference an
existing named secret in the workspace). Omitting both registers a connection
with no secret (or, on update, keeps the existing one).

delegated.description: B3a: run BI queries as the caller's per-user engine JWT (delegation).

governed.description:
The data behind this connection is governed at the engine (Ranger row
filters / column masks). Publishing a Data API endpoint onto it — or
previewing one against it — requires `delegated` or
`options.impersonate`; see [`Database::governed`].

# Why this one field is `Option` on a body where nothing else is

`PUT /ws/{ws}/databases/{id}` is a WHOLE-ROW update: every field of this
body is written, so an omitted field is written as its `serde` default.
For `name` or `port` that is merely an API a client must send in full.
For a security flag it is a control that a client which predates the
field — a script, an IaC provider, a `curl` recipe copied before this
shipped — **silently turns off by editing a port**, with a 200, nothing
logged, and the endpoints on that connection quietly un-gated. That is
the same failure class the flag exists to prevent: a protection that
depends on every writer remembering it.

So `None` means "leave it as it is" and only an explicit `false` clears
it. Absence cannot clear the control; clearing is a thing a client says.
The keep-current semantics live in the SQL (`COALESCE($n, governed)` in
[`crate::registry::repo::DatabaseRepo::update_in_workspace`]) rather than
in a read-modify-write here, so there is no window between reading the
old value and writing it back.

On CREATE there is nothing to keep, and `None` is `false` — the same
direction migration 0130 defaulted the column to, for the reason stated
there: it is the value that changes nothing, not the value that is
safest.

DatabaseListDto.description:
Minimal listing for the Explorer DB picker (no connection internals).

**Nothing constructs this today.** `GET /ws/{ws}/databases` answers
`Vec<DatabaseDetailDto>`; this type survives only as a published schema
component. Adding a field here therefore ships a documented field that no
response ever carries — Package 1 added `governed` to it and the field was
dead on arrival. If a caller needs a narrower listing, give `list` this
return type first; until then, leave it alone.

groupby.description: Usable as a groupby dimension in charts.

filterable.description: Usable as a filter in charts.

semantic_type.description: Semantic role driving smart rendering and chart defaults; "" = none. Rejected with 400 if not one of the listed values.

DatasetDataBody.description:
Body of the object-scoped dataset data-preview: an OPTIONAL row cap only.
There is deliberately NO client SQL field — the endpoint always runs
`SELECT * FROM <the dataset's own source>`, so a shared reader can preview
only the dataset its grant covers. Unknown fields are ignored.

limit.description: Rows to preview. Clamped to [100, 1000]; defaults to 200 when absent.

certified.description: Certified as a trusted/official dataset (for a list badge).

DatasetUsageDto.description: A chart that uses a dataset (for the dataset Usage view).

DeleteBackfillsRequest.description: Delete up to 100 backfills, each on its own.

seconds.description: Soft-delete retention in seconds; null = hard delete.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the denied request.

conditions.description:
Each entry, in declaration order. `null` in the workspace list (the
drawer reads the per-flow route).

oneOf.description: The open window; `null` when none is open (an ended one is none).

DiscoveryDoc.description:
OIDC discovery document served at `/.well-known/openid-configuration` so the
embedded lakekeeper can locate this IdP's JWKS + token endpoint. Doc-only
mirror of the `serde_json::Value` the handler builds.

EndpointSnapshot.description:
What a published version freezes. Self-contained on purpose: P4's serving
path must be able to answer a request from this alone, without reading the
draft row.

**This type is read back out of an immutable column.** M2 does not migrate
`dataapi.endpoint_versions.snapshot` and must not: a published version is
the contract a live consumer is already coding against, and rewriting frozen
rows to suit a newer binary is the one thing "frozen" is supposed to
prevent. The compatibility therefore lives in the READER — see
[`EndpointSnapshotRepr`] — exactly as M1's `#[serde(default =
"default_required")]` on [`ColumnSpec::required`] did.

statements.description:
The endpoint's N SQL definitions, in execution order, each with its own
frozen columns (M1's per-branch union, now scoped to one statement).

Never empty: [`EndpointSnapshotRepr`] refuses a snapshot that carries
neither a `statements` list nor the pre-M2 `sql` + `columns` pair, and
refuses an explicitly empty list.

iterated.description:
Which declared parameters SOME statement iterates — the endpoint's one
shape decision, made at publish and frozen here (package S Task 6).

# Why this is frozen rather than re-derived, and why package S forced it

`serving::params::resolve` used to compute this itself, by scanning every
statement's `sql` for a `{% for x in NAME %}` header
(`render::iterated_params_union`, the one function it shares with
publish). That works only while the text exists before the request does.

**A scripted statement makes it circular.** Its SQL is generated from the
caller's parameters, so there is no text to scan until the parameters are
resolved — and resolving them needs this decision first, because it is
what makes `?regions=EU` a one-element LIST rather than a scalar (a
`{% for %}` over a scalar is "plain is not iterable", a 500 on an
ordinary request). Deriving it from the one template publish happened to
generate would repeat M2's own bug one level down: a set decided from one
text of several, disagreeing with the union publish validated against.

So publish freezes the set it decided across EVERY template of EVERY
statement, and serving hands it to `params::resolve_supplied_with` — the
same entry point preview already uses, for the same reason.

`#[serde(default)]` for the snapshots published before this field
existed. Empty is also what publish writes for an endpoint that iterates
nothing, and the two are deliberately indistinguishable: the reader falls
back to deriving from the written statements' text, which answers empty
in exactly those cases. A pre-S snapshot has no scripted statement (no
path could publish one), so the fallback is complete for every row that
can carry it.

`skip_serializing_if` for the same reason the reader has a default: a
snapshot published before this field existed must round-trip through this
type BYTE for byte, and without it a re-serialised pre-S row gains
`"iterated": []`. There is a single writer today, so nothing re-serialises
a stored row in practice — which is exactly the kind of "harmless today"
that stops being true quietly.

delegated.description:
Whether `database_id` delegated per-user credentials to the engine at the
moment this version was published.

**Half of a witness PAIR — see [`Self::impersonate`], and do not read
this field alone.** Together they are the two mutable columns that decide
whether the engine runs a query as the CALLER, which is the only thing
that makes a shared cache unsafe. An earlier version of this comment, and
of both checks that read it, treated `delegated` as the whole condition;
it is not, and the gap was a live cross-principal leak.

impersonate.description:
Whether `query.databases.options.impersonate` was set at the moment this
version was published. The other half of the witness pair.

**`delegated` alone does not decide whether the engine runs per
principal, and believing it did was a real leak.** `delegation_for`'s
NON-delegated arm still returns `Some(principal_email)` as the session
user (`egret-query/src/execution/mod.rs:86`), and both connectors act on
`options.impersonate` independently of `delegated`:

* `connector/trino.rs:43` — `bearer_token.is_some() || options.impersonate
  == Some(true)` sends `X-Trino-User: <caller>`;
* `connector/starrocks.rs:129` — `bearer_token.is_none() &&
  options.impersonate == Some(true)` issues
  `EXECUTE AS <caller> WITH NO REVERT`.

So `{delegated: false, options: {impersonate: true}}` — which
`DatabaseInput` accepts, the two fields being independent and unvalidated
— runs every query under the caller's own Ranger policy while looking
non-delegated to anything that reads `delegated`.

**Both halves must be compared against the live row before serving from a
shared cache.** Freezing only `delegated` let a `shared` endpoint on such
a connection cache principal A's filtered rows under a principal-less key
and serve them to principal B: a 200, `meta.cached: true`, nothing in
`access_log` to distinguish it, and the witness silent because live
`delegated` still equalled frozen `delegated`.

`#[serde(default)]` so a snapshot written before this field existed
deserialises as `false`. That is the fail-closed direction: such a
snapshot can only have been published against a connection this check now
refuses, so comparing `false` against a live `true` yields
`cache_scope_stale` and a re-publish, which is the correct outcome.

param_gate.description:
Which revision of the publish-time parameter gate this version passed.

**A stamp, not a note.** P4.5's §7 said "every endpoint with parameters
must be re-published after P4.5" — an instruction to an operator, which
is not an enforcement. A version frozen before the gate existed carries
`0` here (`#[serde(default)]`), so the serving path can REFUSE it rather
than render a definition no rule ever looked at. That turns the migration
from something someone has to remember into something the server checks.

An integer rather than a bool, because the situation it exists for is
exactly the one that recurs: when a future revision of the gate closes a
rule the current one misses, bumping [`PARAM_GATE`] makes every snapshot
stamped with the older gate refuse to serve until it is re-published and
re-checked. A bool could only ever say "some gate ran", which is the claim
that was not good enough this time either.

Only consulted when the snapshot declares parameters: a version with no
`params` renders nothing, so there is nothing for the gate to have missed
and nothing to force a re-publish of.

EngineConflictBody.description:
The 409 body for an engine delete/unassign that was refused. `code` is
`engine_has_dependents` (with `dependents`) or `constraint_violation` (with
`constraint`).

EngineDependentDto.description: One (workspace, kind) group of blocking assets, with up to five names.

workspaceSlug.description: For links: the UI routes a workspace as `/explore/{slug}/…`.

EngineDependentKind.description: A kind of asset that blocks deleting or unassigning an engine.

EngineDetailDto.description: `GET /engines/{id}` payload: the engine row flattened with live status.

status.description:
For an external engine this is the row's placeholder `running`, which
means nothing: read `origin` instead (egret does not monitor it).

origin.description:
`provisioned` (egret runs the cluster) or `external` (egret holds a row
for a cluster it never provisions, updates, restarts, scales or deletes).

host.description: External only: the host the engine answers on.

port.description: External only: the port the engine answers on.

image.description:
Provisioned only: the full image ref the engine's stored spec runs (for
StarRocks the FE image; for Trino the `trinoConfig.image` override when
set, else the bare `imageVersion` expanded to `trinodb/trino:<version>`).
Absent when the spec pins none.

rangerPluginVersion.description:
The Ranger plugin version egret reads this engine at. External: the
version the operator declared. Provisioned: the version its exact image
ships (`egret_perm::plugin_version_for_image`); absent when the image is
not one egret has measured.

rangerPluginVersionModelled.description:
Whether egret's Ranger evaluator has been read against this engine's
(type, plugin version) PAIR: only the pairs in
`egret_perm::MODELLED_RANGER_PLUGINS` are. When `false`, a migration to the profile bound to this
engine is refused (never evaluated at a guessed version) and `explain`
answers that it cannot. Enforcement is unchanged.

rangerPluginVersionNote.description:
Why the engine is not modelled, and how to fix it (for a provisioned
engine: pin its image). Absent when modelled.

EngineNotChecked.description: An engine that reaches the classification but was not asked.

reason.description:
Why it was not asked: `external` (egret never connects to an engine it
does not run, and holds no credential for it) or `not running: <status>`
(`provisioning`, `failed` or `deleting`).

EngineSpecDto.description:
The provisioning parameters surfaced back to clients (subset of the stored
`spec` jsonb; internal bookkeeping keys are ignored on deserialize).

trinoConfig.description: Surfaced back so the UI can prefill the config editor on reload.

starrocksConfig.description:
StarRocks equivalent of `trino_config`: the persisted `starrocksConfig`
block (images/replicas/resources/delegation/feConfig/cnConfig/
cnAutoscaling/pod) surfaced back so the UI can prefill the StarRocks
config editor + show KPIs/auth on reload. Absent for Trino engines.

EngineWorkspaceDto.description: A workspace an engine is assigned to (CP `…/workspaces` list payload).

ErrorBody.description:
The JSON body every error response carries: `{ "error": "<message>" }`.

This is the OpenAPI schema counterpart of the body produced by
`IntoResponse for Error` above — the single shape returned for every 4xx/5xx
across the API. Handlers reference it in their `#[utoipa::path]`
`responses(...)` for the error statuses. 5xx messages are redacted to
`"internal error"`; client-facing errors pass their `Display` message.

code.description:
Machine-readable discriminant, present only where clients must branch on
the reason. Currently only `"feature_disabled"`. Omitted otherwise, so
no existing response changes shape.

source.description:
The flow source this execution runs, frozen at start. The plan is pure
over it, which is why a detail page can draw the topology from this
string alone.

runs.description: Every task run, in `run_ix` order — the executor's creation order.

can_manage.description:
Whether the caller may resume and replay this execution: they hold
`workflow:manage` in this workspace. A detail page hides both actions
when this is false; the routes still check for themselves.

effective_labels.description:
What the run sees as `labels`: the flow's, then `labels`, the later key
winning. Empty when the frozen source does not parse.

ExecutionDto.description:
One execution in full: every list field, plus the two things only a detail
page needs — the frozen `source` and every task run, ordered by `run_ix`.

ExecutionGraph.description:
`GET …/executions/{id}/graph`'s answer: the graph of the execution's frozen
source, and the state of every node that has a run.

states.description: Node uid -> its state. A node with no run has no entry.

ExecutionListItemDto.description:
One execution as `GET /executions` lists it.

**No `source`.** It is the whole frozen flow YAML — one document per row —
and a fifty-row page would carry fifty of them to show a column that does
not exist. The field is not merely omitted here: [`ExecutionRow`] does not
have it at all, so no future edit to this DTO can put it back by accident.
`GET /executions/{id}` carries it, because a detail page draws the topology
from it.

`workspace_id` is dropped for the reason every other DTO in this module
drops it: the `{workspace}` path segment already named it, and a body field
that merely echoes the URL is a second place for it to be wrong.

flow_id.description:
The draft this execution came from, and `NULL` only if something
outside this crate issued a real `DELETE` — **trashing a flow does not
clear it**, because `FlowRepo`'s delete is soft and nothing in
`egret-workflow/src` issues a `DELETE FROM`. A trashed flow's
executions are still listed, and still findable by `flow_id`.

flow_key.description: The YAML's own `id`; `flow_id` is taken by the draft's uuid above.

history.description:
The state timeline, as stored: an array of state NAMES, e.g.
`["CREATED","RUNNING","SUCCESS"]`. It carries no timestamps — see
[`TaskRunDto::history`], which is written by the same function.

execution_trigger.description: The trigger record, `NULL` for an API start.

replayed_from_execution_id.description:
The execution this one is a manual replay of (`POST …/replay`), `NULL`
for every other start. A `CREATE_NEW_EXECUTION` retry is NOT linked
here; it carries `parent_execution_id` instead.

started_at.description:
The first time the execution entered `RUNNING`. `NULL` before it runs,
for one that never ran (an SLA that cancelled it at creation), and for
an execution recorded before these times existed — a UI shows that last
case as estimated, never as "not started".

ended_at.description:
When the execution entered a terminal state; `NULL` while it has not
(a paused execution has none), and for an execution recorded before
these times existed. Written once: later writes to a finished
execution do not move it.

labels.description:
The labels this execution was started with beyond its flow's own
`labels:` (a backfill's, a replay's copy); `null` for none. Not the flow's.

backfill_id.description: The backfill that fired this execution (W7f), `null` otherwise.

ExecutionPageDto.description:
One page of executions, with the size of the whole match behind it and the
window that was actually served.

**`limit`/`offset` are echoed because they are CLAMPED**, and a clamp
nobody can see is the indefensible one (the same reasoning
`egret-dataapi`'s `ActivityCallsQuery::limit` states). A caller that asks
for 1000 rows is told it was served 200 rather than having to infer it from
a short page — which it could not, since a short page is also what the last
page looks like.

total.description:
Every execution matching the filter, not just this page's. Counted by a
second statement carrying the same predicates, workspace one included.

limit.description: The page size actually used, after the clamp.

offset.description: The offset actually used, after the clamp.

ExplainAccess.description:
One Ranger ACCESS TYPE's verdict inside one profile.

**A `write` explain is several of these, and they are never collapsed.**
