Ranger has no `write`: `AccessRequest.access_type` is one string, and
`egret_perm::engine_accesses` maps `write` to `insert,delete` on Trino and
`insert,update,delete` on StarRocks. An operator who can insert but not
delete has to be able to see that, which one merged verdict cannot say.

access_type.description:
The Ranger access type evaluated, verbatim — `select`, `insert`,
`update`, `delete`.

decision.description:
What `egret-ranger-eval` answered for the artifact this profile serves.
Three-valued on purpose: `Undecidable` names what stands between the
evaluator and a defensible answer rather than guessing in either
direction.

oneOf.description:
The deciding policy's `perm` model object, or `None` — see
[`ExplainAttribution`]. Always `None` for `Undecidable`, which has no
single deciding policy.
`perm-grant-{uuid}`.

`perm-rule-{uuid}`, or `perm-rule-{uuid}-{locator}` for StarRocks'
per-column expansion, where ONE `perm.rules` row becomes N policies and
the locator is the only thing that says which expansion decided.

`perm-clearance-{tag_id}[-{locator}]`. A clearance has no Ranger
analogue on the wire, so `tag` and `required_roles` are reconstructed
here from the `tags` row the name points at (`tags.key`, not
`tags.name`) and from `classification_policies`. `tag` is `None` when
the tag row is gone — a compiled clearance can outlive its gate until
the next recompile, and inventing a name for it would be worse than
saying none is known.

**`required_roles` is `None` when no gate could be looked up, and that
is why it is an `Option` rather than a list.** The gate is keyed by
`tags.key`, so when the `tags` row is gone there is no key to look one
up by and nothing is known about the clearing roles. An empty list
would state the opposite — that the gate names no role — which SP4d-2a
measured live and found false: the gate declared `['sp4d2a_cleared']`
and the page said it declared only groups. `None` makes "we could not
look" unrepresentable as "there is nothing to find".

**This is an honest 3→2, not 3→3.** `Some([])` still carries two facts
this wire cannot separate: (1) the gate declares only
`required_groups`, which compiles to no engine deny at all (D2/D7), and
(2) there is no `classification_policies` row for the tag at all —
`clearance_gates_for_tags_via` filters on
`cardinality(cp.required_roles) > 0` and `clearing_roles` turns a miss
into an empty list, so a DELETED gate whose compiled clearance
policy is still being served reads exactly like a groups-only one.
Separating those two needs a second query that distinguishes "no row"
from "row with no roles"; until something asks for it, the page says
both out loud.

required_roles.description:
`None` = no gate was looked up because `tag` is `None`.
`Some(roles)` = the lookup ran, and an empty `roles` is a fact
about the gate rather than about the lookup. `attribution_for` is
its only producer, via `clearing_roles`.

oneOf.description:
`perm-clearance-mv`: a StarRocks profile's engine-wide `create
materialized view` deny (view governance A3). Its exceptions are the
users cleared for EVERY classification with a column on the profile,
so it names no single tag.

ExplainAttribution.description:
The `perm` model object the DECIDING policy's Ranger NAME maps back to —
[`crate::attribute_policy_name`], resolved per decision.

**`None` on the owning [`ExplainAccess`] is a real answer, not a gap.**
Four live categories of policy have no model object at all — the
`egret-admin`/`all` hierarchies auto-bind seeds onto every generated
profile, `egret-engine-mgmt`'s delegator plumbing, operator-written raw
JSON, and Ranger's own `superuser` short-circuit — and every one of them
can decide a real request. They are reported by their Ranger name and id on
the decision itself and never dropped: dropping what egret's compiler does
not own is exactly the blindness this endpoint was rerouted to remove.

ExplainMask.description:
The data-mask verdict for the target column: Ranger's `select` request
evaluated as a masked read.

access_type.description: Always `select`: a mask is applied to a read.

oneOf.description:
The deciding mask policy's `perm` model object, as for an access verdict;
`None` for no mask or an undecidable answer.

ExplainOutcome.description:
Which of `explain`'s two shapes a response carries.

**"No engine serves this catalog" is not a refusal.** Collapsing it into a
`Denied` would tell a steward the model is withholding an access when in
fact no plugin is ever consulted about the resource — nothing is enforcing,
which is a different fact. `profiles` is empty for exactly this outcome,
and this discriminator exists so a client never has to infer a
security-relevant fact from the absence of data (an empty list also reads
as "we did not look").

ExplainProfile.description:
One policy profile's answer: the artifact ITS plugin downloads, evaluated
for its own engine.

Per profile rather than once overall because a single answer cannot be
right for two: the same `perm` grant compiles into two different policy
sets, the two engines do not share the resource-level vocabulary the
request is built from (`schema` vs `database`), and their access-type
vocabularies are only partly the same.

service_name.description:
`policy.authz_services.name` — the name the plugin polls
`/service/plugins/policies/download/{service}` with.

tags.description:
The tag set **this profile's** verdicts could have been decided by.

# ⚠ This lives on the PROFILE, and the move is the fix for three defects at once

**Whole-branch review, H1 / H2 / H3 — one defect in three costumes: a
value computed once per REQUEST, presented as though it were per-verdict.**
It was `ExplainResponse::tags`, one list for the whole response, and the
page rendered one heading under all profiles. Each costume was measured:

* **H3, and reachable with no StarRocks, no second profile and no tag
  service at all.** The list was returned even when `profiles` is EMPTY,
  so a catalog nothing serves rendered "Nothing is enforcing" and "Tags
  that decide this request — pii" on one screen, with no verdicts in
  existence. `catalog_tag_assignments` has no catalog column, so a sibling
  catalog's assignment on the same warehouse resolves for this target too.
* **H1.** A catalog served by one profile with a tag service and one
  without made the page say, once, that these tags decide this request —
  false for the second, where nothing tag-related decided anything.
* **H2.** A StarRocks profile given a `tagService` would list tags as
  deciding while `enriched_tags` discards every one of them.

Fixing the three sentences would have left a fourth instance free to
appear. **With the set on the profile there is nowhere to put a tag list
except beside a verdict**, so `no_profile_serves_the_catalog` cannot carry
one — the payload the H3 probe rendered is now unrepresentable.

**The F4/F5 property is kept, not traded.** This is still ONE resolution,
`resolved_tags_for_target`'s, computed once before the loop and the same
object every verdict was evaluated against — not a second query. What
differs per profile is only the ONE narrowing this crate can apply
soundly: see below.

# What the narrowing is, and why it cannot drift from the evaluator

Empty when [`ExplainProfile::tag_policies_in_download`] is `0`. That is a
ONE-WAY implication, not a reimplementation: with no tag policy of any
kind in the download, the evaluator's `of_kind` is empty for every policy
type and no tag can reach any verdict, so an empty list here cannot
disagree with it. The evaluator's actual per-access-type rule stays the
evaluator's; reproducing it here would be the second-copy shape this
package has refused four times.

⚠ **A non-empty list does NOT claim the tags were evaluated** — H2's drop
happens inside `enriched_tags`, against this profile's own service-def,
and is not visible from here. The page's wording is held to that: the set
is what this profile's plugin resolves, and which verdict a tag decided is
on the verdict's own attribution.

tag_policies_in_download.description:
How many tag policies **this profile's download** carries —
`tagPolicies.policies.len()`, or `0` when there is no tag block at all
because the profile has no bound tag service.

Carried so the page can say WHY a profile's tag set is empty while the
column is tagged — the question H1's steward is left with otherwise — and
it is the predicate [`ExplainProfile::tags`] is narrowed by.

oneOf.description:
What the engine masks the target COLUMN to for this subject — where a
StarRocks clearance shows (view governance A2). The clearance is a
per-column deny AND a priority-1 data mask that applies through every
view. For an uncleared reader the mask is `MASK_NULL`, and then the deny
is not consulted: see [`ExplainProfile::masked_read_skips_access`].

Present only for a `read` explain of a COLUMN on a StarRocks profile. A
table-level target has no column to mask, a `write` has no masked request,
and Trino's masks come from the tag service, which the evaluator refuses
(tier c), so none is asked there.

masked_read_skips_access.description:
`true` when StarRocks consults no access policy for the target column:
a `read` of a column whose deciding mask is `MASK_NULL`, from whichever
policy (final review V-1, live §3.4 cases 2a/2b/2c; a hand-written
`MASK_NULL` with a hand-written deny measured too, §4.4 case 3a). The read returns
`NULL` for the column whoever denies it, so
[`ExplainProfile::accesses`] carries no `select` verdict and
[`ExplainProfile::mask`] is the answer.

What this cannot say is the query-level consequence: the query as a
whole is still refused unless the reader may select another column it
reads, and when it selects only such columns StarRocks checks the
table's first unmasked column (measured: `id` on a partly classified
Iceberg table, live result §3.4 case 2a) or `___count___` for
`count(*)` (§3.4 case 2a). When no column is unmasked, on an Iceberg
table it checks the hidden `_file` / `_pos` columns, so a no-grant
reader of a fully classified Iceberg table is refused (§4.4 case 3b).
Explain does not know the query's other columns.

Any other mask type keeps the `select` verdict (`MASK_HASH` was measured
checked; the rest are unmeasured), and so does no mask. When the mask
verdict is undecidable the access verdict is kept and is provisional: if
StarRocks applies a `MASK_NULL` there, it does not check that access.
Never set on Trino, which checks access on a masked column.

(Explain no longer answers `create materialized view`, Task 12 M-4: the
A3 deny is engine-wide, so no single database's verdict says more than
the rule, and the database it asked about held nothing.)

ExplainResolvedTag.description:
One tag egret resolved for the target, and **where the attachment that
produced it lives** — which is the half of the answer F4 measured missing.

# ⚠ Why this is a bool and not the evaluator's `MatchType`

`MatchType` has five variants and `attachment_for` can produce only two:
`Self_` for an attachment naming the column, `Ancestor` for one that stops at
the table. Putting the enum on the wire would need a word for three states
this path cannot reach — and inventing wire vocabulary for an unreachable
state is how the `clearance_required` string got rendered raw for two
releases.

So this reads back the field the mapping actually WROTE:
`attached_through.levels` is exactly what `attachment_for` built from
`from_assignments`' rule, and `column` is in it iff the attachment names the
column. One datum, read once — not a second derivation from a parallel
source, which is the two-comparisons defect this package has hit four times.

name.description:
`tags.name` — the identifier the tag download carries as the tag's `type`
and therefore the one the engine matches tag policies on. **Not
`tags.key`**, which is what this field used to report and which can
differ: live, the key and the name differ for one of three tags.

attached_at_column.description:
`true` ⇒ the assignment names this column (Ranger `SELF`). `false` ⇒ it
stops at the table and reaches this resource as an `ANCESTOR`, so the row
to change is the TABLE's, not this column's. For a target that names no
column this is always `false` and says nothing extra — the attachment and
the target are the same resource.

ExplainResponse.description:
What `explain` answers with: one verdict block per profile serving the
target's catalog, over the SERVED ARTIFACT.

oneOf.description:
Why `explain` declined to resolve this target's tags — absent when it
resolved them.

**This exists because the REASON was unreachable (fix round 3, IMPORTANT 1
/ LOW 3).** The evaluator's `UndecidableCause::TagsUnresolved` is a unit
variant and says only "the caller did not resolve", which is all the
evaluator can know; `resolved_tags_for_target` declines for more than one
state and the states have different remedies and different REACHES, and
`.is_some()` at the call site threw the distinction away. The page then
rendered round 1's single sentence for every one of them — naming a stored
row that does not exist, and claiming a per-catalog reach for the state that
is per-REQUEST. (There were four states when that was measured; migration
0177 made two of them unrepresentable and left two.)

**Carried here rather than as a payload on `TagsUnresolved`**, which was
the other option: `egret-ranger-eval` is a pure crate that knows nothing of
`catalog_tag_assignments`, and the reason is a property of egret's STORAGE
and of this REQUEST, not of the evaluator's input. It is also per
target-and-catalog rather than per access, so the response is where it is
true exactly once. The 1:1 pairing is a property of one function: this is
`Some` exactly when the handler passed `resolved_tags: None`, which is the
only production state in which the evaluator raises `TagsUnresolved`.

ExplainSubject.description:
The caller `explain` decides about.

**It carries a `user` and nothing else**, and each of the three fields it
has lost was removed — never merely ignored — for one version of one
reason: a caller-supplied value cannot be allowed to stand in for a fact
only egret can verify.

**No `workspaces` field (SP4a Task 15, D3 defect 2).** It used to be
caller-supplied, `#[serde(default)]` to `vec![]`, and the retired model
evaluator trusted it verbatim — so a caller naming just a `user` (the
natural way to call this endpoint) silently got `denied` for every
`workspace_members` grant, however real the compiled Ranger policy made
that access; the live gate measured exactly that. SP4a's fix was for
`explain` to resolve the memberships itself. Under SP4d-2a there is nothing
left to resolve: a `workspace_members` grant reaches the artifact already
expanded into usernames by `crate::members::expand_enumerated_principals`,
so the subject's memberships are not an input to the answer at all.

**And no `roles` field either (SP4c Task 7 — the same defect, on the field
next to it).** The SP4c live gate
(`docs/en/plans/2026-09-28-sp4c-live-result.md`) measured both directions of
it: naming only a `user` returned `clearance_required` for the subject the
engine had just served the classified column to, and
`{"user":"analyst","roles":["sp4c_cleared"]}` returned `allowed` for the
subject the engine refuses — a caller asserting a role it does not hold was
believed, so the diagnostic could be told a lie and would repeat it. SP4c
fixed it by reading the subject's roles from `access_grants`. SP4d-2a keeps
the same rule by a stronger means: the evaluator is sent NO roles at all
(see below), so there is nothing to assert and nothing to filter. **This is
not a "what-if" endpoint**: D9 (SP4b) defines it as answering why a subject
**is** allowed or refused, and a field that let a caller invent the
subject's clearance would answer a different question while looking
authoritative.

**And no `groups` field either, as of SP4d-2a Task 5 — the third field
removed from this struct for the third version of one reason.** Until this
task `groups` was caller-supplied and matched by the model evaluator, on
the argument that the UI said so. `explain` now answers with the artifact
the engine downloads, and `roles` and `groups` reach that evaluator EMPTY:
egret serves no `/service/roles/download` and runs no usersync, so a Ranger
policy item naming a role or a group matches nobody on any engine egret
provisions (D0/D7), and Ranger's `public` — the one group name that DOES
match everybody — matches whatever the request carries. A field whose value
can change no answer is a field that lies about what the endpoint does, so
it is gone rather than ignored, exactly as `workspaces` and `roles` were.

Sending no roles at all is also the strongest available form of SP4c's rule
that a caller may not assert a role the subject does not hold: there is no
role to assert. A request that still carries `groups` is accepted and the
key ignored (nothing here sets `deny_unknown_fields`), so an older client
keeps working while answering the same question everyone else gets.

oneOf.description:
A stored assignment value carries one of the characters on which the two
case folds can disagree — see [`FOLD_DIVERGENT`].

The TARGET carries one of those characters. **Per request, not per
catalog** — nothing is stored wrongly and every other target in the catalog
answers normally.

ExplainTagDecline.description:
Which of the two states made `explain` decline to resolve the target's tags
— see [`ExplainResponse::tag_resolution_declined`] and
[`stored_coordinate_is_fold_divergent`].

The two have two different REACHES, which is the whole reason they are carried
apart: the first is a property of stored data and holds for every target in the
catalog until that row changes; the second is a property of the request and
holds for nothing else.

⚠ **This carried FOUR variants until SP4d debt Task 3.** `StoredLevelEmpty` and
`StoredWildcard` were the other two, and migration 0177's
`catalog_tag_assignments_levels_are_present_and_literal` makes both states
unrepresentable: no running egret can read such a row, so no response can
report one. They are removed rather than left unreachable — an API variant a
client must still branch on for a state that cannot occur is the same defect as
a superseded comment. The enumeration of what the matcher does and the schema
now forbids survives on [`stored_coordinate_is_fold_divergent`], which is where
the next person needs it.

The stored variant carries the offending coordinate so the page can name the
row to fix. That is a `policy:read` surface already — the response's `tags`
field reports attachments on the target — and naming no row is what produced
the measured defect: a sentence telling a steward to re-store an assignment
that was already stored on a table.

ExplainTargetLevel.description: Which level of the target [`ExplainTagDecline::TargetFoldDivergent`] is about.

FeatureDto.description: One module and whether this workspace has it switched on.

size.description: The file's size in bytes, as indexed when it was stored.

previewable.description:
`false` (with no rows) for a file that is neither Ion nor UTF-8 text,
Ion that does not parse, or Ion nested deeper than 100 levels.

rows.description:
`.ion`: one JSON value per top-level Ion value (a struct's null fields
omitted, a timestamp as its Ion text, a decimal as a number). Anything
else: one string per line.

truncated.description:
More rows follow than `maxRows`, or the preview's byte budget
(`workflow.storage.max_read_bytes`) ended the read.

value.description:
Comparison operand. Scalar for most operators; a JSON array for `in`/`not_in`;
ignored for `is_null`/`is_not_null`. Validated against the column's generic type.

FindingDto.description:
A validation finding, over the wire. Mirrors [`Finding`] field for field;
a separate type only because `Finding::code` is `&'static str` and this
crate's DTOs derive `utoipa::ToSchema`, which `Finding` itself does not
(it is a `models`/`spec` type and must stay HTTP-agnostic, per this
crate's own module boundary — see `lib.rs`'s doc comment).

FlowDto.description:
A flow draft, over the wire — everything `GET /flows/{id}` promises: the
source, the stored plan, and a validation report computed fresh from
`source` (see this module's doc comment on why it is never stored).

created_by_name.description:
The creator's display name: the profile name, else the email. Null
when `created_by` is null or the user no longer exists (W7a spec §7.4).

latest_version.description:
The flow's highest version number; null when it has none. Versions
are snapshots to compare and restore: executions run the saved draft
(W7a spec §4, §5.3).

can_manage.description:
Whether the caller may save, publish, run and delete this flow: they
hold `workflow:manage` in this workspace. An editor opens read-only
when this is false; every mutating route still checks for itself.

FlowGraphRequest.description: `POST /flows/graph` body: the unsaved YAML to draw.

FlowListItemDto.description:
A flow draft as `GET /flows` lists it — no `source`/`plan`/`validation`:
re-parsing and re-validating every draft in the workspace on every list
call is the wrong cost to pay for a list view, and the list route was
never asked to answer "is this flow currently valid" (`GET /flows/{id}`
is).

created_by_name.description:
The creator's display name: the profile name, else the email. Null
when `created_by` is null or the user no longer exists (W7a spec §7.4).

latest_version.description:
The flow's highest version number; null when it has none. Versions
are snapshots to compare and restore: executions run the saved draft
(W7a spec §4, §5.3).

states.description: The source states it hears, after defaults.

not_listening_reason.description:
Why a trigger without `dependsOn` has no listener row: it does not
resolve.

FlowTriggersDto.description: A flow's triggers, in declaration order.

flow_disabled.description: The flow's YAML says `disabled: true`, or its `state` is `disabled`.

flow_deleted.description: The flow is in the trash: every trigger is effective-disabled.

scheduler_enabled.description: This deployment runs the schedule loop.

worker_enabled.description: This deployment runs the worker (and the Flow-trigger processor).

FlowVersionDto.description: A published version, over the wire.

created_by_name.description:
The publisher's display name: the profile name, else the email. Null
when `created_by` is null or the user no longer exists (W7a spec §7.4).

GatedProfile.description: One profile the gate evaluated, and the artifact diff the engine will see.

probes_full.description: Probes the unpruned gate would have evaluated.

pruning_fallback.description: Why pruning gave the full set, when it did.

removed_policies.description: Policy names (resource and tag) the download no longer serves.

added_policies.description:
Policy names the download now serves that it did not. A compiled name
embeds its grant or rule id (`perm-grant-<id>`), so when `committed` is
false that id is the rolled-back write's and is never stored; the real
migration's compiled policies are named when written.

Grant.description: One row of `perm.grants` plus its principal subtract (`perm.grant_principals`).

service_account_id.description: The service account to grant. Must live in this workspace.

GrantOrigin.description:
Why a grant exists. `WorkspaceAssignment` rows are written by the
assignment path, not by a human, and are recreated from the assignment on
demand (D3) — `perm.grants` enforces at most one such row per
`(catalog_id, workspace_id)` via `grants_one_per_assignment`.

GrantView.description:
A grant as the READ surface returns it: the stored [`Grant`], unchanged,
plus the display name of the catalog its `scope.catalog_id` points at.

**Why the name belongs on the payload (SP4b-2 finding 1).** These routes
gate on `policy:read`; `GET /control-plane/catalogs` gates on
`catalog_registry:read`. The Data permissions page rendered its one primary
column — D5's "a grant reads as a sentence" — by resolving `catalog_id`
against that second endpoint, so for a holder of `policy:read` alone (the
very persona the page was built for) the sentence degraded to
`role analyst cannot read 4a8fe34a-….sales.orders`. A page's main feature
must not need a permission that page's own gate does not require. The
compiler already resolves id→name internally (D6) — the backend knew this
name and simply never told the client.

**`#[serde(flatten)]`, so the wire shape stays flat** — `{...grant,
"catalog_name": "wh"}`, one object, and a field added to `Grant` tomorrow
appears here with nothing to update. The same idiom
`DataApiEndpointListItemDto` and `EngineDetailDto` use; utoipa renders it
as an `allOf`, which makes the generated TS type assignable to `Grant`.

`scope.catalog_id` is untouched: it is what a write sends back. This adds,
it does not replace. `catalog_name` is `None` only when the catalog row is
gone (an id whose catalog was deleted under a cascade this read raced) —
never a fabricated or key-derived stand-in.

ImpersonationDto.description:
The active impersonation as surfaced by `/me`: who is being acted-as
(`target`), the admin behind it (`impersonator`), and the overlay's bounds.

expires_at.description: Optional hard expiry. Absent means the client lives until revoked.

IterationRun.description:
One iteration of the `Loop` the execution ran itself, as one node of its
body saw it (W7c Task 6, fix round 1).

state.description:
THIS NODE's state in the iteration: its runs there, folded by
[`FOLD_PRIORITY`] -- not the iteration's own state, which another body
task can decide.

child_execution_id.description: The iteration: the child execution of the graph's execution that ran it.

run_id.description:
The node's run, when the iteration ran it exactly once; null when a
nested `Loop` ran it in several deeper iterations.

total.description: How many iterations this node ran in: `runs.len()`.

by_state.description: Iterations by their folded state's wire name: `runs` counted by `state`.

runs.description:
The node's own run in each iteration it ran in, by `loop_index`. An
iteration where the node never ran has no entry.

JoinableWorkspaceDto.description: A workspace a user may request to join (they are not already a member).

JwksDoc.description:
JWK set served at `/.well-known/jwks.json`. Doc-only mirror of the
`serde_json::Value` the handler builds; each key is a raw RFC 7517 JWK.

type.description: The stored type (never re-inferred on read).

value.description:
The value: a DATETIME as `2025-01-02T03:04:05Z`, a DATE as
`2025-01-02`, a DURATION as Java prints it (`PT24H`), a decimal with
every digit, a JSON value as itself; any JSON type.

type.description:
`STRING`, `NUMBER`, `BOOLEAN`, `DATETIME`, `DATE`, `DURATION` or `JSON`:
the type stored with the latest revision.

size.description: The stored value's size in bytes (its Ion text).

updated.description: When the latest revision was written.

namespace.description: The ancestor namespace the key is read from.

KvKeysBody.description:
The bulk delete's request and answer: the keys to delete, and the keys
that were live and are now deleted (ascending).

deleted.description:
The key was soft-deleted at this revision (its latest); the revision
is still served by `GET …/kv/{key}?revision=N`.

expired.description: This revision has expired: it is not served.

LastExecutionDto.description: The newest execution this trigger started.

LineageReader.description: One view or materialized view that reads the object.

catalog.description:
The registry catalog name for a view; `default_catalog` for a
StarRocks materialized view, where StarRocks keeps every one.

engine.description: The StarRocks engine holding a materialized view; `null` for a view.

matchedBy.description:
`lineage` for a view (its recorded lineage); `baseTable` or `text` for
a materialized view, as the classification page matches them. `text`
means the view has no base-table map and its definition names the
catalog and schema: it may over-report.

LineageState.description: What egret has recorded of a Trino view's lineage (spec B1).

LineageTableRef.description: A recorded base table of a view.

LogLevel.description:
A log line's level: slf4j's five, which are `Log.java`'s `level:` and
Kestra's stored `level`. Stored as `smallint` 0..=4 (the table's CHECK), so
`min_level` is a plain `>=`.

LogLineDto.description:
One stored log line. `task_id`, `task_run_id` and `attempt` are all `null`
for a line about the execution rather than one run; `attempt` is 0-based,
as Kestra's is. A line longer than 15,360 characters was stored as several
consecutive lines (W11 D6), so there is no `truncated` flag.

id.description: The cursor value: strictly increasing in the order lines are served.

ts.description: When the line was produced, by the worker's clock.

LogPageDto.description: One page of an execution's log.

items.description: In `id` order, at most `limit` of them.

next_after.description:
The last returned `id` -- the next call's `after` -- or `null` when
nothing was returned (keep the `after` you sent).

execution_state.description:
The execution's state (Kestra's wire spelling, `RUNNING`, `SUCCESS`,
...), read on this call. For display: **do not stop polling on a
terminal state alone** -- see `complete`.

complete.description:
The execution is terminal AND became so more than the 2 s settle lag
ago. **Stop polling when `complete` is true and `items` is empty**:
then every stored line has been served. A terminal `execution_state`
alone is not enough -- the run's last lines may be younger than the
settle lag and not served yet.

MatchedBy.description: How a view was matched to the classification.

oneOf.description:
Present when the caller is currently impersonating another user (an active
admin overlay resolved to the target). `null` for an ordinary session.
One statement — every endpoint published before M2, and most after it.

columns.description:
The FROZEN columns from the snapshot, not the ones this execution
happened to return. The published contract is what a client codes
against; if the underlying table has drifted, the difference is a
defect to surface, not something to paper over by reporting today's
shape.

oneOf.description:
Several statements, keyed by name — the same keys, in the same order, as
`data`.

statements.description:
Serialized as a JSON OBJECT, from a `Vec` rather than a map, for one
reason: the order is the author's, stated by the list they published,
and it has to be the order `data` uses. A `BTreeMap` would sort the
names and make `meta` disagree with `data` about the sequence for
every endpoint whose statements are not alphabetical.

No key can be lost to another: publish refuses two statements of one
name (`validate_statements`), which is the same guarantee
`statements_data` rests on one level up.

MetaContract.description:
What `meta` reports about the published contract, keyed the only way the
endpoint's statement count permits.

An enum rather than four `Option` fields: `{row_count, columns}` and
`{statements}` are the two legal fillings, and a struct with all of them
optional can also represent both at once and neither at all — two states in
which a client would have two readings of one contract that can disagree.

**`Several` is what Task 7's `meta.columns` could not express.** Until this
existed the field held every statement's frozen columns CONCATENATED in
statement order: complete, but unkeyed, so a caller holding
`["id","name","total"]` could not learn which statement declared which — and
had no way to notice the question was unanswerable.

policy_names.description: Names of policies of THIS profile, exactly as stored.

dry_run.description: Run everything, report it, and roll back.

MigrateResponse.description: What a migration (or its dry run) did, and the proof.

committed.description:
Whether the transaction committed. `false` for every dry run and for
every migration the gate did not prove.

equivalent.description: The gate ran over every affected profile and found no disagreement.

refusal.description:
Why the gate refused to answer at all (no disagreement list is a proof
then). Absent when it answered.

policies.description: Each migrated policy and the model objects it became.

profiles.description:
EVERY profile the gate evaluated — the source and every other profile
the new objects compile into — with what changed in its download.

probe_evaluations.description: Probe evaluations run (probes × plugin versions, over every profile).

disagreements.description: Every probe on which a profile answers differently after the write.

notices.description: Consequences to read before committing (see the module doc).

grant_ids.description:
The grants it became. When `committed` is false (a dry run, or a
migration the gate did not prove) these ids belong to a write that was
rolled back and will never exist: a real migration assigns new ids when
it writes. Use the count, not the ids, to describe a preview.

rule_ids.description: The rules it became; the same caveat as `grant_ids`.

MigrationRecord.description: One `perm.migrated_from` row, as the classifier and the page read it.

policy_name.description:
The policy's name when it was migrated (it may have been renamed
since; provenance is keyed by policy id).

probes_proved.description: How many probe evaluations agreed when the migration was proved.

MissedTicksDto.description: Ticks due and not fired, counted up to 1,000.

more.description: `true`: there are more than `count` (the UI says "1000+").

ModelledRangerPluginDto.description: One modelled (engine type, Ranger plugin version) pair.

NamespaceDependenciesDto.description: A namespace's flow-to-flow graph, built from the flows' saved drafts.

nodes.description:
The namespace's flows and its children's, then every flow elsewhere
with a direct edge to or from one of them; by namespace, then flow id.

edges.description:
Edges with at least one end in the namespace; one per (source,
target, kind).

unparsable.description:
Drafts in the WORKSPACE (not only this namespace) whose YAML does not
parse. Each is still a node (`unparsable: true`) when it is in the
namespace or an edge reaches it, but its own edges are unknown.

NamespaceDependencyKind.description: What an edge of the dependencies graph means.

NamespaceDependencyNodeDto.description: One flow of a namespace's dependencies graph (W7d spec §3.4).

id.description: The flow's id (the uuid every flow route takes); edges name it.

disabled.description:
The flow is switched off: its state is `disabled` or its YAML says
`disabled: true`.

in_namespace.description:
The flow is in the namespace or beneath it (dot-anchored); false for a
flow elsewhere present only for an edge to or from one that is.

dynamic_subflows.description:
`Subflow` tasks whose `namespace` or `flowId` is an expression
(`{{ }}`/`{% %}`): only an execution knows their target, so they draw
no edge.

unparsable.description:
The flow's saved draft does not parse: it is drawn so edges into it
show, but its own edges are unknown.

NewEngineCatalog.description: One catalog to attach when the engine is created.

primary.description:
Exactly one catalog in the list carries this, and it must be an egret
warehouse catalog: the engine's Ranger role and (for StarRocks) its
builtin storage are derived from that warehouse, and since SP3c-2 they
are read back through this attachment rather than off the engine row.
A primary naming a catalog with no warehouse is refused, with the
reason, before anything is created.

NewGrant.description:
A grant as authored over HTTP.

**There is no `origin` field, and that is deliberate.** `perm.grants.origin`
distinguishes a human's `explicit` grant from a `workspace_assignment` row
the assignment path owns and recreates from the assignment on demand (D3),
and `grants_one_per_assignment` allows at most one of the latter per
`(catalog_id, workspace_id)`. A human-authored grant is always `explicit`;
letting a request claim `workspace_assignment` would let the HTTP surface
mint rows the assignment sync believes it owns, which it would then
silently delete or refuse to recreate.

NewRule.description: A named rule as authored over HTTP. `id` is minted by the database.

NewSecret.description:
Request shape for creating a brand-new named secret inline while registering a
connection (storage or database): `{ "name": ..., "value": ... }`. The value
is plaintext, accepted only on write and never returned. Shared across the
HTTP layers so each connection type can mint a named secret in one request.

value.description: Plaintext secret value; accepted only on write, never returned.

id.description:
The id this tab already has. Same contract as [`CardInput::id`]: a hint, honoured only when
the tab already belongs to this dashboard.

Tabs need it for a reason cards do not: `dashboard_cards.tab_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so
recreating a tab took every card on it with it — the cards were being deleted twice over.

canonical_type.description:
The FQCN for a flowable or `Subflow` (whichever spelling was
written) and for a registry type (its canonical row); otherwise
the type as written.

NodeKind.description: The node's kind, serialised as the `node` tag beside its fields.

NodeState.description: One node's state (module doc, "One run, or a fold").

attempts.description: The run's attempt count; for a fold, the most any one run took.

run_id.description: The run's id; null for a fold.

oneOf.description: Set when the runs live in `Loop` iterations.

child_execution_id.description:
For a `Subflow` node's single run: the newest child execution it
started. Absent for any other node, and for a fold.

detail.description: A sentence for the page. Never the engine's own error text.

NotListedReason.description: Why a level was not listed.

deleted.description:
The path was soft-deleted at this revision (its latest); its bytes are
still served by `GET …/files?path&revision`.

path.description: The stored path: a leading `/`; a directory's ends with `/`.

revision.description: The latest revision; always 1 for a directory.

created.description:
When the latest revision was written; `null` only for the namespace's
virtual root (`stats` with no `path`), which has no row.

NsFileUploadForm.description: One part, `fileContent`: the file's bytes, streamed to the namespace file at `path` as its next revision. A `.zip` is stored as one file, never expanded.

ObjectGrantBody.description: Body of a share grant: give `principal` a workspace `role` on this object.

principal_id.description: A user's email, a group's name, or a UUID.

role.description:
`ws_viewer` (Viewer, read) | `ws_editor` (Editor, manage). For a "Blocked"
grant, send `ws_editor` with `effect="deny"`.

effect.description: `allow` (default) | `deny`. A deny blocks the principal on this object.

expires_at.description:
Optional expiry (RFC3339). `None` = never expires (unchanged default).
Enforced at read time by the PDP/admission predicates, not here.

ObjectGrantDto.description: A single object-scoped grant on the object.

principal_name.description:
Human-readable grantee name: a user's email or a group's name. `None` if
the principal row could not be resolved (e.g. deleted).

expires_at.description:
Optional expiry (P2a). `None` = never expires. This is the object's own
direct-grant list (manage-only), so an expired grant is still listed
here — only the read-time admission predicates exclude expired grants.

Optional expiry (RFC3339). `None` = never expires. This is the
management roll-up, so an expired grant is still returned (not filtered).

readers.description:
The views and materialized views that read this table. See
`readers_incomplete`.

oneOf.description:
Set when `readers` may be missing some: a view of this egret catalog
has unknown lineage (failed or not yet computed), egret's views or an
engine's materialized views could not be listed or were not asked, the
catalog is not egret's (its own views are not tracked), or the object
is a view.
Set exactly when the object is a view.

OidcStepUp.description:
`409` body returned when an OIDC-provider admin starts an impersonation: the
client must redirect the browser to `authorize_url` to complete a fresh IdP
re-authentication (`prompt=login`) before the overlay is created (Task 8). The
`code` lets the SPA branch on this specific response.

authorize_url.description: The OIDC authorize URL (carries the sealed impersonation intent in `state`).

envelope.description:
Whether the response carries the `{status, message, data, meta}` wrapper
(`"wrapped"`, the default) or `data`'s value on its own (`"bare"`) —
spec §4.4.

Defaulted rather than made an `Option`, and defaulted to the WRAPPER, so
that every snapshot frozen before this field existed reads back as
`wrapped`: the migration sets no rows and an unpublished endpoint cannot
change shape by being re-read.

`bare` is the success path only. A refusal still answers with
`ServingErrorBody`, because an unwrapped error would be a bare `null` —
nothing at all about what went wrong — under a status this toggle does
not reach.

A `String` like `shape` and `naming`, but — unlike them — **checked
before it is stored**, by [`validate_envelope`]. Serving still falls back
to the documented default and logs rather than refusing (see
`serving::router::envelope_of`), because a frozen snapshot must keep
answering; the check exists so no new row can reach that fallback. See
[`validate_envelope`] for why this field and not its two neighbours.

oneOf.description: Absent means no transform, which is every snapshot frozen before C2.

OwnerDto.description:
A schedule owner. The owner is a security-relevant field, not decoration:
the alert's query runs with this user's permissions at run time (§5.2).

ParamSpec.description:
`deny_unknown_fields` on the author-supplied config types.

`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on the request-body struct does NOT reach a
nested one, and the nested one is where the damage was: posting the
documented-but-wrong `{"rate_limit": {"per_client_qps": 5}}` returned 201
with `per_key_qps` silently defaulted to `0`. A rate limit the author
believes they set and did not is worse than an error.

Applied to the six types an AUTHOR fills in — [`ParamSpec`], [`CacheSpec`],
[`LimitsSpec`], [`RateLimitSpec`], [`OutputSpec`], [`StatementSpec`] — and
deliberately NOT to [`EndpointSnapshot`], [`ColumnSpec`] or
[`StatementSnapshot`], which the server writes for itself and where a typo
is impossible.

**The cost, stated because it is a real constraint on a persisted format.**
These types are also how a stored `jsonb` column is read back. Adding a field
in some future version and then rolling the binary back would make the older
code refuse to deserialize rows the newer one wrote, as a 500 on read. That is
a loud failure rather than a silent one, and it is the standard price of
strict deserialization; a future field that must be readable by older code has
to be introduced some other way.

allowed.description:
Required when `ty` is `Enum`. The ONLY safe form for anything that
reaches an identifier position — see spec §3.

minimum.description:
Inclusive lower bound for a `Number`. Ignored for every other type, and
publish refuses it there (see `check_constraints`).

**A string, not an `i64` or `f64`, and deliberately.** `coerce` already
refuses to put a decimal through an `f64`, because a decimal that
round-trips through a float stops comparing equal to itself on the
engine. A bound stored as a float would reintroduce that on the
comparison side.

maximum.description: Inclusive upper bound for a `Number`. See [`ParamSpec::minimum`].

min_length.description:
Minimum length for a `String`, in **Unicode scalars, not bytes**. A
`max_length: 10` that fails a Vietnamese name at seven letters is a bug
the author cannot see from the declaration.

pattern.description:
A regex the **whole** value must match, for a `String`.

Anchored implicitly: `is_match` is a search, so an unanchored `"abc"`
would accept `xxabcxx`, which is not what an author writing a validation
rule means. An author who writes their own `^…$` gets the same answer.

not_before.description:
Inclusive earliest value for a `Date` or `Timestamp`.

**Stored exactly as the author wrote it**, in any spelling the declared
type parses — an unpadded `"2026-1-1"` is the same instant as
`"2026-01-01"` and is enforced identically, because publish and `coerce`
both normalise the bound before comparing it. This field is therefore
NOT guaranteed to hold the spelling `coerce` produces.

The spelling still reaches one reader unchanged: the generated OpenAPI
document quotes this string RAW in the parameter's description, so
`"2026-1-1"` is what a caller is shown — the right instant in a shape
the endpoint never answers with. Prefer the canonical `%Y-%m-%d` (or
`%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S%.f`) spelling so the published contract reads the way
the endpoint replies.

not_after.description:
Inclusive latest value for a `Date` or `Timestamp`. See
[`ParamSpec::not_before`].

PermPrincipal.description:
One principal reference. `r#ref` is the bare identifier egret's D7
measurement settled on for users (a username, never an email) — the store
writes it through unchanged for every kind.

**The OpenAPI name is `PermPrincipal`, not `Principal`, and that is a
bug fix** (SP4a Task 10, finding 2). `egret-policy`'s admin surface
already exports a DIFFERENT `Principal` — the policy picker's
`{kind, name, label}` row (`egret-policy/src/admin/mod.rs`). Two distinct
Rust types deriving `ToSchema` under one schema name collapse into one
entry in the merged document, and the picker's won: every `$ref` from
`PrincipalSet` — and so every `NewGrant.principals` — resolved to
`{kind, name, label}`, a shape this type cannot deserialize. A client
generated from the committed `openapi.json` could not construct a grant at
all. The two names are now distinct, and each DTO refs its own.

PolicySummary.description: Flattened, UI-facing view of one stored Ranger policy.

managed_by.description:
Who owns the row (migration 0180): `"operator"`, `"compiler"` or
`"infra"`. The server refuses edits, toggles and deletes of an
`"infra"` row, so the profile page withholds those controls.

PolicyWarning.description:
One finding about a stored policy's resource levels (SP4d-4 Task 11).
`kind` is `select_stops_above_column` (with `level`: the deepest level the
policy names) or `level_gap` (with `missing`: the absent level that has a
named level beneath it); each carries the `sentence` an operator reads.

PolicyWriteWarning.description: One warning on a policy write's response (`kind: "evaluation_order_changed"`).

policyId.description: The other policy's id, when known.

allOf.description:
What is in the editor right now — not what is stored. **The only
statement this route runs.**

The author's SQL, or the Starlark script that builds it. A script is
generated here through the same generator publish and serving use, and
what it produced comes back in [`DataApiPreviewDto::generated_sql`].

siblings.description:
The SQL text of the endpoint's OTHER statements, as they are on screen.

They decide ONE thing and are used for nothing else: whether a parameter
arrives as a scalar or a list, which is a property of the endpoint (any
statement's `{% for %}` header makes it a list) and not of the statement
being previewed. They are never rendered, bound or executed. Omit the
field for a one-statement endpoint. At most `MAX_STATEMENTS - 1` of them,
since `sql` plus its siblings is an endpoint.

params.description: The parameter declarations as they are on screen right now.

values.description:
The author's test values, one list per parameter name. A list, not a
scalar, because a repeated parameter is a list on the serving path too
and preview must resolve it the same way.

output.description:
The response contract as it is on screen — carried for ONE part of it,
`transform`, and applied to nothing.

`shape`, `naming` and `envelope` are still not applied here (see
[`DataApiPreviewDto`]); they arrive because `transform`'s own publish
rules are stated in terms of them — a transform beside a non-default
`shape` is refused — and reconstructing an `OutputSpec` from a bare
`TransformSpec` plus defaults would be a second, quietly weaker copy of
[`crate::lifecycle::check_transform`]. The whole struct goes in, and
that one function decides.

database_id.description:
The database picker's current value. Workspace-scoped by
`connection_safety`, which answers `NotFound` for a database
belonging to another workspace — this id comes from a request body, so it
is exactly the shape that could name someone else's connection.

PreviewEndpointInput.description:
The on-screen draft, as the request carries it.

No `cache`, `limits` or `rate_limit`: preview does not consult any of them,
and accepting fields it ignores would invite the reader to think it did.
# Unknown keys, `sql`-or-`script`, and why [`Deserialize`] is hand-written

Package S Task 7 gave this body the same two-case source
[`egret_dataapi_api::StatementSpec`] has, flattened onto the object the same
way: `{"sql": …}` or `{"script": …}`, never both and never neither. That
shape and `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` are the pair serde documents as not
composing, so this impl states all three rules itself — exactly what
`StatementSpec` does, for the reasons measured there. A body an older client
sends is unchanged: `sql` is still `sql`, in the same position, with the same
type.

PreviewRequest.description:
What `preview` is asked to try — SP4b D2.

It is the create body plus an optional `id`, rather than a separate shape,
because the preview runs the REAL write: anything the preview could accept
and a write could not would be a lie by construction. Exactly one of `grant`
and `rule` must be present; two optional fields rather than a tagged union
so the generated client is one plain object with two optional members.

id.description: Present ⇒ preview a PATCH of this existing row. Absent ⇒ a create.

PreviewResponse.description:
What the write WOULD have done. `compile` is the same summary the write
itself returns, produced by the same recompile — this endpoint rolls that
work back rather than recomputing it.

Principal.description: One egret identity offered by the policy picker.

name.description:
The value written into the raw-JSON Ranger policy editor (user email /
group name). Deliberately unchanged by `username` below — that editor
surface is Ranger-native and an email can be the right value there.

username.description:
The user's allocated bare username (`users.username`, minted by
[`egret_auth::users::UserRepo::ensure_username`]) — this is the value
the engine actually sees (SP4a D7 measured `current_user` as `admin`,
never `admin@egret.local`). `None` for a `group` principal, and for a
`user` principal that has never triggered allocation. Never guess this
by slugifying `name`/`label`: `ensure_username` lowercases, slugifies,
*and* appends `-2`/`-3`/… on collision, which no client can reproduce.

PrincipalKind.description:
`perm.principal_kind`. `WorkspaceMembers` is measured, not assumed (D7):
Trino has no group provider and egret never pushes one, so a `group`
principal matches nobody inside the engine today. `WorkspaceMembers`
exists here for a later task to expand into the member list enumerated at
compile time; nothing compiles it yet.

PrincipalSet.description:
A principal subtract: `include` minus `exclude`. This is what lets egret
drop Ranger's allow-exception/deny-exception blocks from the authoring
surface (see `crates/egret-perm/tests/store.rs`) — both `Grant.principals`
and `Rule.exempt` use it, and both round-trip through a `(kind, ref, mode)`
table (`perm.grant_principals`, `perm.rule_exemptions`).

ProfileDto.description: A profile (Ranger service) + the engine(s) that link to it.

tag_service.description:
The classification-tag policy service this Trino profile carries its
tag-based masking/row-filters in: the profile's OWN `config.tagService`,
resolved to a real profile. `None` when the profile carries no link or
the link names nothing — the FE shows a "Tags" tab only when this is set.

**SP4d debt Task 9 fix round:** this no longer falls back to the
`<name>_tag` naming convention. It is the same answer
`usable_tag_service` gives before letting an engine bind, and the same
one the plugin download serves, so a tab is offered only when a tag
policy authored in it could actually be enforced.

origin.description:
`"manual"` (hand-authored, fully editable) or `"generated"` (compiled
by the SP4a permission model from its grants and rules).

**Exposed because D4's requirement is that the profile says so BEFORE
an edit is overwritten, not after** (whole-branch review, Important 4).
The raw-JSON policy editor still ships in SP4a and is still the only
policy UI, and a `'generated'` profile is now only PARTLY frozen — its
`perm-*` policies are compiler-owned and refuse an edit with a 409,
while foreign policies in the same profile stay editable. Without this
field the editor cannot tell an operator which half they are looking
at, and the first thing they learn is the 409 on save.

ProfileWarnings.description:
The `policyId`-keyed answer of `GET .../warnings`: how many warnings the
profile carries in all and which policies carry them.

ProposedObjects.description:
How many model objects a migratable policy becomes. No `clearances`:
clearance migration is out of scope ([`Blocker::ClearanceNotExpressible`]).

PublishEndpointInput.description:
The `POST /publish` body. Every field optional, so `{}` is a valid publish —
of a version that breaks nobody.

note.description: Free-form "what changed", stored on the version.

acknowledge_breaking.description:
The acknowledgement issued by `POST …/validate` for the breaking changes
this publish would make, required only when there are some.

# Why this is a token and not `force: true`

A boolean can be set once, in a deploy script, by someone who has never
read a diff — and every breaking publish that script ever makes is then
pre-approved, silently. There is no constant to hardcode here: the value
is a digest of the breaking changes themselves, mixed with the endpoint
and the version currently live, so it cannot be produced without having
been handed the list it acknowledges, and one issued for yesterday's
break does not match today's. Acknowledging accidentally is not a
discipline this field asks anyone to keep; it is not reachable.

Sending one when the publish breaks nothing is refused too, rather than
ignored — an acknowledgement that does not correspond to anything is a
stale one, and staying silent about it is how a client learns to send it
always.

PublishFlowRequest.description:
`POST /flows/{id}/publish` body. Optional in the request (a bare `POST`
with no body publishes with an empty note), following
`PublishEndpointInput`'s own optionality in `egret-dataapi`.

QueryParam.description:
A single SQL-Lab template parameter. `value` is substituted for `{{name}}`
as a typed, escaped SQL literal (never raw text) so parameters cannot inject.

temporal_units.description:
dimension column name -> temporal unit token (snake_case, e.g. "month", "day_of_week").
Empty (default) = no truncation = legacy behavior.

QueryStatusDto.description: Full status view (preview inline; full result via the results endpoint).

columns.description: Column metadata `[{name,type}]`; `null` until the query finishes.

preview.description: Inline preview rows (bounded, row-major); `null` until the query finishes.

RangerErrorBody.description:
Doc-only mirror of the Ranger error envelope (`{ msg, statusCode }`), which
differs from the control-plane `ErrorBody` shape.

RangerPluginConfigDto.description: The Ranger plugin configuration an external engine's admin installs.

serviceName.description: The bound policy profile: the Ranger service name the plugin asks for.

downloadUrl.description:
`{public_url}/service/plugins/policies/download/{serviceName}`: where the
plugin's download lands. The files below carry `public_url` itself (the
plugin appends the path).

authMode.description:
`anonymous`, or `bearer-configured` (egret requires a bearer token on
`/service`; the token is never shown here).

rangerPluginVersion.description: The plugin version the engine was DECLARED to run.

rangerPluginVersionModelled.description:
Whether egret's evaluator models the (type, version) pair. When `false`,
migrations into this profile are refused.

warnings.description: Things that make the install not work, or not safe, as configured.

assumptions.description:
What egret's `explain` and migration gate assume about the plugin and
cannot check on an external engine.

adminMustSupply.description:
What the admin must supply themselves. egret renders no credential and
invents none.

RangerPluginFileDto.description: One file the admin of an external engine installs.

name.description:
File name; for StarRocks `fe.conf (add this line)` is a line to add to
the FE's existing `fe.conf`, not a file to replace it with.

RangerServiceDefs.description: Doc-only mirror of the `{ "serviceDefs": [...] }` envelope `list_defs` returns.

serviceDefs.description: Each element is a raw Ranger service-definition object (stored verbatim).

RangerServicePolicies.description:
Doc-only mirror of the `ServicePolicies` plugin download envelope
(`egret-policy-api`) returned by `download_policies`.

policies.description: The service's enabled policies, each a raw Ranger policy object.

RangerServiceTags.description: Doc-only mirror of the empty `ServiceTags` payload returned by `download_tags`.

tags.description: Tag map keyed by numeric tag-id → tag-def instance.

resourceToTagIds.description: `{ "<resourceId>": [<tagId>, ...] }` linking each resource to its tags.

ReadersIncomplete.description: Why the reader list may be missing some.

detail.description: A sentence for the page. Never an engine's own error text.

RecipientDto.description:
A delivery destination. `config` is kind-dependent — `{"addresses": [...]}`
for email, `{"url": "...", "secret_id": "..."}` for webhook — and is
validated against `kind` on the way in.

RecipientInput.description: A recipient as submitted; the id is assigned by the server.

RecipientKind.description: Where a firing schedule delivers to.

name.description:
Unique across engines. Lower-case letters, digits and `-`, 1 to 63
characters, starting and ending alphanumeric.

host.description: Host or IP the engine answers on: no scheme, no port, no path.

port.description: Trino's HTTP port or StarRocks' FE query port.

rangerPluginVersion.description:
The Ranger plugin version installed on the engine, `x.y.z`, one of the
Ranger 2.x releases. **Only the pairs in
`egret_perm::MODELLED_RANGER_PLUGINS` are modelled by egret's evaluator**
(a type and version PAIR; the refusal sentence names them): any other is
stored as declared, and a migration to a profile bound to this engine is
then refused rather than evaluated with the wrong semantics.

authzServiceId.description:
A policy profile to bind. Its type must equal `type`, no other engine may
bind it, and a Trino profile needs a usable `tagService`.

catalogs.description: Registry catalogs to declare attached. Nothing is applied to the engine.

RegistryCatalogDto.description:
A registry catalog. `config` is the typed per-kind configuration (snake_case
fields, spec §4.2); it never holds a plaintext secret.

warehouseId.description: The warehouse an egret catalog is.

configError.description:
Why this row's stored `config` no longer parses, if it does not.
A stored row the tightened validator now refuses stays visible and
repairable instead of vanishing — and, critically, never fails the
whole list (SP3c-1 review N1).

RenderCard.description:
One card's IDENTITY and query shape — no rows.

Step one of the render. The page needs the saved spec to resolve the
dashboard's parameters against it, which it cannot do if the server has
already run the query.

param_mappings.description:
`dashboard_cards.options.paramMappings`: parameter id -> the column on
THIS card it filters. A parameter with no mapping here does not apply to
this card, which is why the mapping travels per card rather than once
for the dashboard.

RenderCardData.description: One card's DATA. Step two, once the page has resolved the filters.

RenderCardRequest.description:
What the page asks for in step two: the resolved dashboard-parameter
filters for one card.

The same shape as `egret_bi`'s `CardRunBody`, and merged the same way —
onto the card's SAVED spec, never replacing it. A client supplies FILTERS,
never a query: each `col` is checked against the dataset's real columns by
`compile_chart_sql` -> `chartquery::build` -> `find_column`, and each
temporal unit against the `TemporalUnit` enum. Accepting a whole spec here
would let whoever holds a render token run arbitrary SQL as the schedule's
owner.

parameters.description:
The dashboard's parameter definitions, verbatim. The print page resolves
them to filters with `applyParamsToChart` — the SAME module the
interactive dashboard uses — and sends the result back to
[`run_cards`].

Ported to Rust instead, this would be a second implementation of six
text operators, relative date windows and month/quarter/year arithmetic
that must agree with the first one exactly, forever. When they drifted,
the emailed image would quietly stop matching the dashboard — which is
the bug this whole path exists to fix.

`null` for a chart report: a chart has no parameters.

ResourceTagBody.description:
Body of an assign/unassign: the resource (`column` optional ⇒ table-level) +
the tag id.

ResourceTagDto.description:
A catalog resource tag on the wire (snake_case). `column` is empty for a
table-level tag. The tag itself is nested under `tag` (the full P3.1 tag
shape, matching the FE `Tag` type) so the browse UI can read `a.tag`.

ResultsPage.description: A page of the full result.

rows.description: Row-major cell values; each element is one row (a JSON array).

parentRoleId.description:
The role this one inherits permissions from (same scope). `None` at the
top of a chain.

inheritedPermissions.description:
Effective-minus-own permissions, for read-only display. Populated on the
single-role GET; empty on the list endpoint.

RollbackEndpointInput.description:
The `POST /rollback` body: name the version by NUMBER or by ID, not both.

`version` is scoped to the endpoint by construction — version numbers are only
unique within one endpoint's history — so that spelling cannot name another
endpoint's version even in principle. `version_id` is a bare uuid and
therefore CAN, which is precisely why the store's statement carries
`v.endpoint_id = e.id`. Both exist because a UI listing versions has their ids
to hand while a human types a number.

Rule.description:
One row of `perm.rules` plus its exemption set (`perm.rule_exemptions`).

**`exempt` is a full `PrincipalSet`, including `exclude`, but the
compiler cannot express `exclude` here.** The model, the store, and the
OpenAPI schema all accept it — `perm.rule_exemptions` has the same
`mode` column `perm.grant_principals` does, precisely so "exempt this
whole group except these people" round-trips the way a grant's subtract
does. But `egret-perm-compile`'s `rules::compile_rule` refuses any `Rule` whose
`exempt.exclude` is non-empty (`CompileError::UnexpressibleExemption`):
unlike an access-policy item, a Ranger masking/row-filter item
(`MaskItemInput`/`RowFilterItemInput`) has no allow/deny-exception block
to put a subtract in, so there is no correct Ranger shape for it. The
same is true of a `Role` principal in `exempt` (those item types have no
`roles` bucket at all). This makes `exempt.exclude`/`Role` an authorable,
storable shape that can never compile — a limitation an authoring UI
should surface when the rule is written, not one a steward discovers as
a 500 the first time the rule is compiled.

RuleKind.description:
`perm.rule_kind` plus its type-dependent payload, CHECK-constrained in the
database (`(kind = 'mask') = (mask_type IS NOT NULL)`, etc.) and made
unrepresentable here instead.

catalog_name.description:
`registry.catalogs.name` for a `path` selector's catalog; `None` for a
`tag` selector.

tag_name.description: `tags.name` for a `tag` selector's `key`; `None` for a `path` selector.

RuleView.description:
A rule as the READ surface returns it: the stored [`Rule`], unchanged, plus
whichever display name its selector needs — see [`GrantView`] for why the
resolution happens here and not in the client.

A rule's selector is one of two shapes, so exactly one of these is ever
`Some`: `catalog_name` for a `path` selector (the same resolution a grant's
scope gets), `tag_name` for a `tag` selector. A tag rule stores `tags.key`
(`pii`) because that is the stable identifier (D6), while a steward reads
the display name (`PII`) — and `GET /tags` needs `tag:read`, which
`policy:read` does not imply either.

RunDto.description: One entry in the run-log drawer.

RunState.description:
Superset's five run states, verbatim. They are the vocabulary that makes the
list page legible — in particular `noop` ("ran, condition false") and `grace`
("would have fired, suppressed") are the two answers to "why didn't I get an
email?", and collapsing either into `success` loses that answer.

folder_id.description: Folder this saved query lives in (`None` = root). Serialized as a string.

ScheduleDetailDto.description:
The editor's view: everything on the summary plus the type-specific blocks,
recipients, and the advanced knobs.

message.description:
A user-authored note carried into the notification body. Distinct from
`description`, which is the line the LIST shows.

message_footer.description:
The closing note, rendered UNDER the result — `message` opens the
notification, this one closes it, and an inline image sits between them.
Defaulted, so a client written before 0116 keeps working unchanged.

skip_if_empty.description: Metabase's `skip_if_empty`: send nothing when the run produced no rows.

targets.description:
Objects a REPORT delivers, in page order. Empty falls back to the
single `chart_id`/`dashboard_id`, which is every pre-0115 row.

ScheduleInfoDto.description: A `Schedule` trigger: its YAML and its `workflow.triggers` row.

next_evaluation_date.description: The next tick the scheduler will fire. `null` with `off_queue`.

evaluated_at.description: The last tick the scheduler processed.

last_error.description: Why the schedule went off the queue, when it did.

off_queue.description:
`true`: no next date; the schedule does not fire until a save
re-initialises it (`last_error` says why).

oneOf.description:
On the queue and overdue (`next_evaluation_date <= now`, which a
switched-off schedule becomes, since it keeps its date): the ticks from
`next_evaluation_date` through now. During a backfill, the regular
ticks waiting instead: from `backfill.previous_next_evaluation_date`
through now. `null` otherwise.

recover_missed_schedules.description:
The YAML's `recoverMissedSchedules` as written (`ALL`, `NONE`, `LAST`);
`null` when absent, which a re-enable treats as `ALL`.

ScheduleSummaryDto.description:
One row of the list page.

`last_state` is the column the page exists for, so it is on the summary
rather than the detail — a list that needs a second request per row to say
whether anything is broken would not be opened.

can_manage.description:
Whether the caller may edit/delete schedules in this workspace.

One workspace-level answer repeated on every row, not a per-object
decision — `alert:manage` is workspace-scoped, so the answer is the same
for the whole list. It exists because the client CANNOT derive it: a
session's `permissions` carries PLATFORM grants only, so a UI that
guessed would show a reader destructive controls that 403 on click.

bookmarked.description: Whether the CALLER has starred this one — per-user, unlike `can_manage`.

folder_id.description: The folder this row is grouped under, or `None` for "Uncategorized".

deleted_at.description: Set only in the trash view; `None` for a live schedule.

ScheduleType.description:
What a schedule does: evaluate a query (`alert`), deliver a rendering of a
saved object (`report`), or watch a Data API endpoint's traffic
(`dataapi_alert`, migration 0128).

SchemaColumn.description: A single column in a DESCRIBE result.

Scope.description:
A path into a catalog. `schema`/`table`/`column` narrow progressively —
`perm.grants` and `perm.rules` both CHECK that a level cannot be skipped
(a column implies a table implies a schema).

SearchHit.description:
A schema-object search hit (a table/view matched by the SQL Lab global
object search). `catalog` is empty for engines without a catalog level.

SecretDto.description: Response DTO mirroring `WorkspaceSecretMeta` (never exposes the plaintext).

SecurityMode.description:
A Trino view's security mode, read from its stored `trino.run-as-owner`
property and never from the statement.

SeedResult.description: Doc-only mirror of the `{ "created": <n> }` body `seed_defaults` returns.

created.description: How many default policies were created (0 if the profile already had any).

Selector.description:
What a rule's scope is selected by. `Tag` references `tags.key` — never
`tags.name`, which is mutable and non-unique (D6) — and egret never emits
a tag *access* policy for it (D2); only masking/row-filter rules select by
tag. `Path` is a `Scope`, same shape as a grant's.

ServingErrorBody.description:
The serving surface's error envelope (spec §7).

Named `ServingErrorBody` and not `ErrorBody` on purpose. `egret_core::http`
already exports an `ErrorBody`, it is a DIFFERENT shape (`{"error":
"<string>"}`), and `egret_server::openapi_doc` merges this crate's serving
document with the rest of the API into one OpenAPI document — where two
schemas sharing a name silently overwrite each other. A generated client
would then be typed against whichever won.

status.description:
Always [`ServingStatus::Error`] here, and DERIVED from the status this
response will actually carry rather than written as a constant — see
[`ServingStatus`]. `status` mirrors the HTTP status; it never replaces
it, and a body saying `"error"` under a `200` is the failure mode the
mirror exists to make unrepresentable.

message.description:
The same human-readable string as `error.message`, lifted to where the
success envelope carries it (`null` there) so that `status` and
`message` are readable on EVERY serving response without knowing first
which of the two bodies arrived.

`error.code` is what a client branches on and is untouched; this is the
human half, and it may be reworded.

code.description:
The stable, machine-readable code from spec §7. Clients branch on this;
`message` is for humans and may be reworded.

message.description:
A fixed string per code. Never rendered from an internal error — see the
module comment.

request_id.description:
The correlation id, also written to `dataapi.access_log.request_id` and
to every `tracing` line for this call. Quoting it is how a caller gets
support to the detail they were deliberately not given.

allOf.description:
Flattened, so the wire carries `{version, cached, request_id, row_count,
columns}` or `{version, cached, request_id, statements}` — never a
`contract` key of its own.

ServingMeta.description:
The endpoint-wide half of `meta`, plus whichever contract shape the
endpoint's statement count calls for.

ServingResponse.description:
The success body (spec §4.4, §5.1.2).

```json
{ "status": "ok", "message": null, "data": …, "meta": { … } }
```

**This replaced the `{data, meta}` body P4 shipped, in one migration rather
than by carrying two shapes.** Endpoints published under the old envelope
have served real traffic since 2026-08-16; the decision to break rather than
version was taken deliberately (spec §4.4) because consumers are few and
internal, the API is pre-1.0, and two envelopes forever cost more than one
migration. It belongs in the deploy note and must not be made silent.

`meta.version` is the published version that served the call, so a
client-side bug is reproducible against the exact snapshot that produced it.
`meta.cached` is likewise not cosmetic: without it a stale-looking result is
indistinguishable from a fresh one while debugging.

status.description:
Always [`ServingStatus::Ok`] here — this type is only built on the
success path — but read off `StatusCode::OK` rather than written as a
constant, so the two cannot drift apart. See [`ServingStatus`].

message.description:
`null` on success. It is the human-readable half of a REFUSAL
([`ServingErrorBody`](super::error::ServingErrorBody)), not a success
banner, and a client that finds a string here is reading an error.

data.description:
The rows for a ONE-statement endpoint — an array of objects (default) or
of arrays, per `output.shape` — and an object keyed by statement NAME for
several.

Not a union at the contract level: `openapi_gen` writes one document per
endpoint and an endpoint's statement count is frozen in its snapshot, so
each generated schema is unambiguous.

The SHARED serving document below describes every endpoint at once, so it
deliberately carries no `value_type`: utoipa then emits the unconstrained
schema for `serde_json::Value`, which is the only honest answer there.
`value_type = Vec<Object>` — what this field carried until M2 — asserted
"array of objects" about a body that is an OBJECT for a several-statement
endpoint.

ServingStatus.description:
`status` in the envelope (spec §4.4).

**It MIRRORS the HTTP status; it never replaces it.** A body saying
`"status": "error"` under a `200` is the failure mode this exists to avoid —
SQLREST answers `200` for everything and pushes the outcome into the body
(`HttpApiServlet.process` never calls `setStatus`), which breaks HTTP caches,
proxies and monitoring, and forces every client to parse a body to learn that
it failed. egret keeps returning real `400`/`403`/`429`/`503`.

So this value is DERIVED from the status line rather than written beside it —
see [`ServingStatus::mirroring`], which is the only constructor. Two
independent spellings of one outcome is exactly the shape that drifts.

required_roles.description:
Clearance role NAMES; a principal needs `>= 1` to access objects carrying
this tag. Cleared = `>= 1` role OR `>= 1` group; both empty = no gate.

required_groups.description:
Clearance GROUP ids (as strings; Access P3.4). Each is parsed as a `Uuid`
before hitting the repo — a non-uuid entry is rejected `400 BadRequest`
(never spliced unvalidated into a Cedar policy string).

SetActiveBody.description:
Flip only `active` (P5's list-row toggle). A dedicated endpoint rather
than routing a toggle through `PUT .../alerts/{id}`, which is a FULL
REPLACE requiring every field — building a toggle on top of it would mean
a read-modify-write that could clobber a concurrent edit to the rest of
the schedule.

SetBackfillsPausedRequest.description: Pause or resume up to 100 backfills, each on its own.

SetDashboardCertification.description:
Body for `PUT /dashboards/{id}/certification`.

A SEPARATE endpoint from the dashboard PUT on purpose: certification is guarded by the
platform-scoped `dashboard:certify`, while editing is guarded by the workspace-scoped
`dashboard:manage`. Folding these fields into `UpdateDashboard` would let any editor certify
their own dashboard by saving it, which is the failure this feature exists to avoid.

details.description:
Free text explaining the certification. Ignored when `certified` is false — withdrawing
clears the note rather than leaving a stale justification attached.

SetDatasetCertification.description:
Body of the dataset / metric certification endpoints. Deliberately carries NO `certified_by`:
the certifier is the session, exactly as it is for dashboards. A client that could name the
certifier could forge provenance, which is the defect 0109 closes.

details.description:
Ignored when `certified` is false — withdrawing clears the note rather than leaving a
stale justification attached to an uncertified dataset.

SetFeatures.description:
The feature keys to change; any key this workspace's catalog entry already
has is left exactly as it is. This is a merge, not a full replacement,
despite arriving over `PUT`: `PUT` is still the right verb because the
operation is idempotent (sending the same body twice yields the same
state) — it is not required to mention every field of the resource. A
merge is also forward-safe: when a sixth module joins the catalog, a
caller that still only sends today's five keys leaves it untouched
instead of implicitly switching it on, which is what a true full
replacement (write/delete a row for every key, mentioned or not) would do.

features.description:
Feature key -> enabled. Unknown keys are rejected with 400 and nothing
is written (`WorkspaceRepo::set_features` validates the whole batch
before opening its transaction). The *resulting* state — this batch
merged onto what is already stored — is also validated against
cross-module dependencies (currently: `dashboards` requires `charts`),
so a body that never mentions `dashboards` can still be rejected if it
would leave `dashboards` on and `charts` off.

folder_id.description: `null` moves the schedule back to Uncategorized.

SetTriggerDisabledRequest.description: Switch one trigger on or off.

recover_missed.description:
On a re-enable of a switched-off, overdue `Schedule` only (an already-on
trigger keeps its dates): `false` (the default)
skips the missed ticks (the next date becomes the first tick after
now); `true` follows the trigger's `recoverMissedSchedules` (absent or
`ALL`: every missed tick runs; `NONE`: skip; `LAST`: the latest one
runs). Ignored otherwise. During a backfill the choice applies to the
regular schedule's resume position, not to the backfill's tick.

SetTriggersDisabledRequest.description: Switch up to 100 triggers on or off, each on its own.

SetWorkspacesBody.description:
`PUT /engines/{id}/workspaces` body: the FULL desired set of workspace ids the
engine should be assigned to (the handler diffs it against the current set).

SkipReport.description:
A grant, a rule, or a tag's classification clearance that a recompile could
not express and left uncompiled. Surfaced
on the response rather than only in the logs: a create that succeeded but
compiled nothing for a service is a fact the author needs at authoring
time, not one a steward discovers from a query that returns no rows.

id.description:
The `perm.grants`/`perm.rules` id — or, for `clearance`, the `tags.id`
whose classification gate could not be expressed (SP4c Task 2).

token.description:
Three-way, like SMTP's password: absent keeps the stored token, `""` is
rejected (a config with no token cannot deliver, so there is nothing
sensible to store), a value replaces it. Required on first write.

SlackConfigDto.description:
What a client may see. There is no token field — not a redacted one, an
ABSENT one, so no future serializer can start including it by accident.

has_token.description:
Always true when a row exists: `token_secret_id` is NOT NULL. It is
reported anyway so the editor's "a token is stored" line reads the same
field on both credential paths — see `redact_recipient_config`.

password.description:
Omitted means "keep the stored password"; `""` means "remove it".

Without the distinction, an editor that renders a blank field (because
it cannot show the real one) would erase the password on every save.

SmtpConfigDto.description:
What a GET returns.

There is deliberately no password field — not even an empty or masked one.
