`has_password` is what the editor needs (to show "configured" and to let the
user keep the existing one), and it is a boolean, so no serialization change
can turn it into the secret.

has_password.description: Whether a password is stored. The password itself is never returned.

to.description: Where to send the probe. Defaults to the configured from-address.

SnippetBody.description: Create/update body for a SQL snippet.

StarRocksConfigBody.description:
Wire shape for `CreateEngineBody.starrocks`: FE/CN image + replicas +
optional per-role resources. Mirrors the `resources{cpuRequest,cpuLimit,
memRequest,memLimit}` shape [`parse_resources`] already understands.

delegationMode.description:
Opt into per-user delegation (Access parity slice 3): `"jwt"` |
`"impersonate"` | omitted/`None` (no delegation — the slice-2 open
engine default). The OIDC coordinates (jwks/issuer) and the
impersonation service-user credential are NOT accepted here — they're
derived from egret's own OIDC config / minted server-side (see
[`create_starrocks_engine`]), same posture as Trino's
`trinoConfig.auth.jwt` vs the delegator secret.

tlsEnabled.description:
Enable FE SSL on the MySQL-protocol port (:9030) when delegation is
configured. Defaults to `true` when `delegation_mode` is set; ignored
otherwise. `false` opts out of TLS while still enabling delegation
(e.g. a dev cluster where the extra listener setup isn't wanted).

feConfig.description:
FE (`fe.conf`) override keys → merged over egret's managed base by the
provisioner. egret-managed keys ([`egret_engine_mgmt_api::SR_PROTECTED_FE_KEYS`])
are rejected up front by [`validate_sr_fe_config`]. Omitted ⇒ preserved on update.

cnConfig.description:
CN (`cn.conf`) override keys → rendered into a ConfigMap by the provisioner.
Omitted ⇒ preserved on update.

cnAutoscaling.description:
CN horizontal autoscaling `{ minReplicas?, maxReplicas, targetCpuPercent? }`.
Stored/read as opaque JSON here; typed into `CnAutoscaling` at provision-req
assembly. Omitted ⇒ preserved on update.

pod.description:
Pod- & container-level scheduling / customization surface (nodeSelector,
tolerations, affinity, sidecars, …). Opaque JSON here; typed into
`StarRocksPod` at provision-req assembly. Omitted ⇒ preserved on update.

feMetaStorageClass.description:
StorageClass backing the FE metadata PVC (`/opt/starrocks/fe/meta`).
Omitted/blank ⇒ the cluster's DEFAULT StorageClass. Omitted ⇒ preserved
on update.

feMetaStorageSize.description:
Size of the FE metadata PVC, as a k8s binary quantity (`"20Gi"`).
Omitted ⇒ preserved on update, then
`egret_engine_mgmt_api::DEFAULT_FE_META_STORAGE_SIZE`.

StartExecutionMultipart.description: `POST .../flows/{id}/executions` as `multipart/form-data`. **Each part is named by an input id.** A part with a file name is that `FILE` input's file: it is streamed to `kestra:///{namespace}/{flow}/executions/{execution}/inputs/{input}/{file name}` and the input's value is that URI. Any other part is a text value. A part naming no declared input, or one named twice, is refused naming it. One start carries at most `workflow.storage.max_file_bytes` + 1 MiB in total.

StartExecutionRequest.description:
`POST .../flows/{id}/executions`'s body. Optional in whole: a flow with no
`inputs:` is started with `{}` and a caller should not have to send a body
to say so.

inputs.description:
The flow's `inputs:`, as a JSON **object**.

**A non-object is REFUSED (400), not coerced.**
[`worker::start_execution_with_trigger`](crate::worker::start_execution_with_trigger)
writes `{}` for anything that is not an object, which is right for a
webhook (whose inputs are rendered, never supplied) and wrong for an API
caller: it would turn `"inputs": [1, 2]` into a silently empty start, and
the author would look for their values in the render context and not find
them. The guard is therefore two-sided and its test is too — `[1,2]` must
400 **and** an absent body and `{}` must both start — because a guard
that only refuses is indistinguishable from one that refuses everything.

password.description: Required for a local-auth admin (step-up). OIDC admins re-auth via OIDC (Task 8).
Required for a local-auth caller (step-up). OIDC callers re-auth via OIDC.

columns.description:
This statement's own frozen columns — see [`MetaContract::Single`]'s
`columns` for why they are the frozen ones.

allOf.description:
The author's SQL, or the script that builds it — flattened, so a
statement frozen before package S reads back byte-for-byte unchanged as
[`StatementSource::Sql`].

StatementSnapshot.description:
The frozen form of a [`StatementSpec`]: what a publish freezes into
[`EndpointSnapshot`] for one statement, its own [`ColumnSpec`] union
included (M1's per-branch column union, now scoped to one statement of N).

No `deny_unknown_fields` — like [`EndpointSnapshot`] and [`ColumnSpec`],
the server writes this for itself; a typo here is not possible the way one
is in a request body.

# It freezes the SOURCE, not the generated text (package S Task 6)

This carried `sql: String` until serving learnt to generate. For a scripted
statement that string was the text `build_sql` returned under publish's
REPRESENTATIVE parameter values — one branch of a script whose whole purpose
is to take a different one per request. Freezing it and serving it would
have made every parameter a scripted statement branches on inert: the
endpoint would answer the representative branch's SQL to every caller, with
a `200` and no error anywhere. So the version freezes what publish validated
— the author's text, or the author's script — and serving generates from it,
per request, with the caller's own values.

**The generated text is deliberately not kept beside the script.** A
statement carrying both a script and a frozen rendering of it is two
definitions with no rule for which one runs — the shape [`StatementSpec`]
refuses at the wire, refused here for the same reason and with a sharper
edge: the failure would be a silent wrong answer rather than an error. What
publish measured about the OTHER branches survives where it is actually
used: `columns` is the union across every template, and
[`EndpointSnapshot::iterated`] is the shape decision made across them all.

oneOf.description: SQL the author wrote, as a template the existing render pipeline runs.

sql.description: SQL the author wrote, as a template the existing render pipeline runs.

oneOf.description:
A Starlark script whose `build_sql(params)` returns that template.

The script decides the statement's STRUCTURE; the values are still the
renderer's. `build_sql` is handed the endpoint's declared parameters and
returns a template with its `{{ }}` intact — every caller value stays a
bind, on exactly the path a hand-written statement's does. Publish runs
it under branch probes to freeze the column contract, and every request
runs it again, so the SQL may differ per call; it may not be a second
path to the engine.

Bounded in length — a publish over the cap is refused with both the
script's size and the cap — and refused if it emits anything but a
single `SELECT`.

script.description:
A Starlark script whose `build_sql(params)` returns that template.

The script decides the statement's STRUCTURE; the values are still the
renderer's. `build_sql` is handed the endpoint's declared parameters and
returns a template with its `{{ }}` intact — every caller value stays a
bind, on exactly the path a hand-written statement's does. Publish runs
it under branch probes to freeze the column contract, and every request
runs it again, so the SQL may differ per call; it may not be a second
path to the engine.

Bounded in length — a publish over the cap is refused with both the
script's size and the cap — and refused if it emits anything but a
single `SELECT`.

StatementSource.description:
Where one statement's SQL comes from: the author typed it, or a script
builds it (package S).

**Two cases and no third.** A statement carrying BOTH a literal and a script
has two definitions and no rule for which one runs; a statement carrying
NEITHER has nothing to execute and would discover that at request time, long
after the author left. Both are refused by the type rather than by a check
someone downstream has to remember — this codebase's repeated lesson is that
unrepresentable beats unforgettable.

The wire form is the ENCLOSING object's key, not a nested one:
`{"name": "rows", "sql": "…"}` or `{"name": "rows", "script": "…"}`. That is
not a style choice. [`StatementSpec`] is the persisted `jsonb` of
`dataapi.endpoints.statements` (migration `0129`) and every row already in
that column is `{"name": …, "sql": …}`, so the text case has to read
unchanged or every list, detail and serve breaks on READ — where no author
is present to see it. A tagged shape (`{"kind": "sql", …}`) would demand a
key no stored row carries.

`Deserialize` is DERIVED here and hand-written on [`StatementSpec`], which is
not an inconsistency. [`StatementSpec`] is a REQUEST body, where "both",
"neither" and a typo are things an author can send and must read a sentence
about; this enum is also read back inside [`StatementSnapshot`], which the
server wrote for itself, where the derive's externally-tagged map is exactly
the stored shape and no message is going anywhere near an author.

allOf.description:
Where this statement's SQL comes from. Flattened onto the object, so the
wire form is `{"name": …, "sql": …}` or `{"name": …, "script": …}` —
the first of those is byte-for-byte what every stored row already is.

StatementSpec.description:
One of an endpoint's N SQL definitions, as an author writes it (M2). The
canonical shape is a `rows` statement and a `total` statement for
pagination, but any number is allowed.

`name` is not decoration: once an endpoint has more than one statement,
the response envelope is a JSON object keyed by statement name and the
generated OpenAPI document names it as a property (M2 Tasks 8-9). A name a
caller writes into their own code is a contract, which is what
[`validate_statement_name`] and [`validate_statements`] enforce —
`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` so the key never needs quoting in JSON and never reads
as private, and uniqueness within the endpoint so the key is unambiguous.

Unknown keys are refused for the same reason as [`ParamSpec`] and its four
siblings: this is a type an AUTHOR fills in, so a typo in the request body
must be a 400, not a silently-ignored field. It is NOT
`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` any more — see the hand-written
[`Deserialize`] impl below for what replaced it and why.

**The PUBLISHED schema cannot state that rule, and this is not an oversight
to fix later.** Flattening makes this an `allOf`, and each branch of an
`allOf` validates the whole object on its own — so an
`additionalProperties: false` branch listing only `name` would reject every
body carrying `sql`, which is all of them. The construct that expresses it
is `unevaluatedProperties`, and utoipa 5.5 cannot emit one (the string does
not occur in its source). So the refusal lives in the reader, where it is
tested; the document states the one-of and loses only the typo class. Same
for [`PreviewEndpointInput`], for the same reason.

StorageDto.description: Response DTO for a storage connection.

StorageInput.description:
Request body for creating/updating a global storage connection. A `new_secret`
takes precedence over a provided `secret_ref`: it mints a new global named
secret and binds the connection to it.

oneOf.description: Mint a new global named secret inline and use it as `secret_ref`.

StoredMember.description: One member of a stored pair, as a steward finds it.

id.description: The rule's id; `null` for a hand-written policy.

policyId.description:
The `policy.authz_policies` id of the stored policy (the one
`PUT /policies/{id}/enabled` takes), for compiled and hand-written alike.

name.description: The rule's name, or the hand-written policy's name.

StoredOverlap.description: One pair already stored in a profile's download.

serviceId.description:
The profile whose download serves the pair (a tag service on its own
when no profile names it).

rules.description: In the pair's order (policy names ascending).

oneOf.description:
Which member Ranger serves today where both match, when that can be
computed; `null` when the order falls to something this report does
not compute (or to the policy name).

params.description:
Template parameters substituted into `{{name}}` placeholders before the
query is sent to the engine.

SweepFailure.description: One view (or one catalog listing) the sweep could not judge.

schema.description:
The namespace, or `None` when the catalog's namespaces could not be
listed.

view.description: The view, or `None` when its namespace could not be listed.

reason.description: Why. The view's tags are unchanged.

retagged.description: Views whose lineage-derived tags it changed.

failures.description: Views (or listings) it could not judge. Their tags are unchanged.

TabularResult.description:
A fully-collected, in-memory query result (bounded by the caller's row limit).

`Serialize`/`Deserialize` are for the E4b contract crate + BI forwarding this
result directly across the seam boundary; today the store persists `columns`
and `rows` individually, so the whole-struct codecs are not yet exercised.

rows.description: Row-major cell values; each inner vec is one row aligned to `columns`.

TagDto.description:
A classification tag carried by an object (Access P3.1). Local snake_case DTO
so egret-bi does not depend on egret-controlplane. `assignment_count` is the
tag's global assignment count (as computed by `TagRepo`).

TaskRunDto.description:
One task run, whole — all twenty-four columns.

Unlike the execution's own row there is nothing dropped here: a detail page
reads ONE execution's runs, so there is no page-sized multiplier the way
`executions.source` has one.

**These are the fields a gantt is drawn from**, and
`tests/executions_routes.rs::a_gantt_row_is_computable_from_the_execution_
dto_alone` computes one from this DTO and nothing else, so W7 cannot
discover a missing field after this package closes. What it uses:
[`Self::task_id`] and [`Self::parent_ix`] for the label and the nesting,
[`Self::state`] for the bar, [`Self::created_seq`]/[`Self::ended_seq`] for
LOGICAL time, and [`Self::started_at`]/[`Self::ended_at`] plus
`attempts[].started_at`/`attempts[].ended_at` for WALL-CLOCK time.

run_ix.description:
The `RunIx` — the executor's creation order, and the order the detail
route returns these in.

task_ix.description: The `TaskIx` — the index into the plan's task list.

type_id.description:
The task's `type:`, and `NULL` exactly when the planned kind is not
runnable — i.e. a flowable the executor drives itself, which is why
such a run has no `attempts` for a gantt to read a start from.

parent_ix.description: The parent run's `run_ix` — a gantt's nesting, `NULL` at the top level.

rendered.description:
The run's rendered expression (an `If`'s condition, a `Switch`'s
value, a `Loop`'s `values:`, ...), `NULL` until it is rendered. For a
`Loop` whose `values:` named a file it is `"<kestra:/// URI>\n<count>"`
-- the file and how many records it holds -- and **never the records**
(W9a Task 11 fix round 1): they are the file's, read through the
execution file API, and stay out of every task-run response.

history.description:
**An array of state NAMES and nothing else** — `["CREATED","RUNNING",
"SUCCESS"]` — written by `worker::claim`'s `states_json`, which maps
each `RunState` to its wire spelling. It is **not** Kestra's
`State.History`, and it carries **no dates**: a timeline drawn from
this alone has an order but no clock. The wall-clock instants are
[`Self::created_at`], [`Self::updated_at`], and `attempts[].started_at`
(milliseconds after the EXECUTION's `created_at`, which is what a
`Tick` is in this engine).

attempts.description:
One entry per attempt: `{"history": [...], "started_at": <ms>,
"ended_at": <ms>}`, both in milliseconds after the execution's
`created_at`. `ended_at` is absent while the attempt is open and on an
attempt recorded before it existed; an attempt that a retry followed
ends no later than the next one starts.

outputs.description:
The run's outputs, `NULL` for a run that has none: a handler that
returned nothing (a `Log`, a `Sleep`) and any run not yet terminal.

created_seq.description:
The executor round this run was created in — LOGICAL time. Two bars
whose wall-clock spans are microseconds apart are still ordered by
this, which is why a gantt wants it beside the timestamps.

ended_seq.description: The executor round this run terminated in; `NULL` while it has not.

started_at.description:
The first time the run entered `RUNNING`: for a worker task, when the
executor handed it to the workers (equal, to the millisecond, to
`attempts[0].started_at`); for a flowable, when the executor first ran
it. Not moved by a resumed pause or a retry. `NULL` for a run that
never ran — `SKIPPED` by `runIf`, or not yet started — and for a run
recorded before these times existed.

ended_at.description:
When the run entered a terminal state; `NULL` while it has not, and
cleared if a retry reopens it. Written once per terminal: a later
write to a finished run does not move it.

TestInput.description: Body for testing an unsaved connection (no `name`).

TlsMode.description:
How the connection is secured. Spelled out rather than inferred from the
port: 587-means-STARTTLS is a convention, not a rule, and guessing wrong
silently sends credentials in the clear.

ToggleRefusal.description:
Why the UI's switch is disabled, the first that applies: the flow is in
the trash, the trigger is not one egret fires, the caller lacks
`workflow:manage`, the YAML disables it.

TokenForm.description:
`POST /oauth/token` form. Which fields are required depends on
`grant_type`, so every field — `grant_type` included — is optional here and
checked by the handler: a missing field is a 400 `invalid_request`, never
the extractor's 422, which no OAuth client reads as a refusal (I4).

subject_token.description:
Required for token exchange: an unexpired access token this IdP issued.
A Bearer `Authorization` header alone does not stand in for it.

TransformSpec.description:
An author's response transform: a Starlark script plus the output schema it
promises.

# Why `returns` is declared rather than inferred

Every other column egret freezes comes from `describe_as`, which works
because a SQL statement's shape is a function of its text and the branch a
parameter takes. A script's shape can depend on the DATA — `if len(rows) > 0`
— which publish cannot see. Inferring from a probe run would produce a
contract that is right for the probe data and wrong for a Tuesday. So the
author declares, publish checks the probes against the declaration, and
serving fails closed on every response that disagrees. See spec §3.

script.description: The script source. Must define `transform(params, statements)`.

returns.description:
The output schema this endpoint promises. `ColumnSpec` is reused rather
than duplicated: its `required` flag already means "present in every
permutation described at publish", which is exactly what it means here.

TriggerEntryDto.description: One declared trigger and its state.

yaml_disabled.description: The flow's or the trigger's YAML says `disabled: true`.

effective_disabled.description:

oneOf.description: Why `can_toggle` is false.

duplicate_id.description:
The flow declares this trigger id more than once (a save-time error,

oneOf.description: `null` in the workspace list.

What a trigger is, as egret runs it: one of the three kinds it fires, or

Flows in scope whose source did not parse: their triggers are unknown

can_manage.description:

flow_uuid.description: The flow's uuid (what the per-flow route and the switch take).

flow_disabled.description:
The flow's YAML says `disabled: true`, or its `state` is `disabled`
(the per-flow route's top-level `flow_disabled`, per row): what makes a

TrinoViewItem.description: One Trino view in the DEFINER audit (spec B5).

securityModeError.description:

server log); `null` otherwise.

owner.description: The DEFINER's `trino.run-as-owner`; `null` for any other mode.

ownerCleared.description:
Whether the owner is cleared for every classification the lineage
reaches. `null` when it cannot be said: not DEFINER, lineage not
computed, or a reached clearance names only groups. Read from current
role membership; the engine enforces the last compile, so after a
grant expires the two differ until the next recompile.

TrinoViewReason.description: Why a Trino view is listed.

params.description:
Values exactly as they would arrive on the query string. A `Vec` per key
because a repeated parameter is a LIST (P4.5), and a trial that could
only send one value could not exercise the case most likely to be wrong.

authorization.description: Always the literal `Bearer ••••`. The token is never serialised.

curl.description: A copyable reproduction using a `$TOKEN` placeholder.

status.description:
The status the SERVING path returned. The trial itself is a 200 whenever
it ran — a 403 from the endpoint is a result, not a failure of the trial.

body.description:
The serving path's own body, verbatim: on success the spec §4.4 envelope
`{status, message, data, meta}` — `data` an array for a one-statement
endpoint and an object keyed by statement name for several — or, for an
endpoint published with `output.envelope: "bare"`, `data`'s value on its
own. On a refusal, spec §7's `{code, message, request_id}`. Verbatim
because the point of the feature is to show what the consumer gets, and a
body this route summarised would be a different answer than the real
one — including about which envelope the endpoint is published in.

notices.description: Consequences that outlive the undo (review I-2).

grants_deleted.description: Model objects the migration created, deleted by the undo.

UnresolvedPrincipal.description: One stored grant principal or rule exemption whose ref matches nobody.

id.description: The grant's or the rule's id.

name.description: The rule's name; `null` for a grant (a grant has none).

ref.description: The ref as stored, byte-for-byte — the string the compiled policy names.

position.description:
`"include"` or `"exclude"` (of the grant's `principals`, or of the rule's
`exempt`).

effect.description: The grant's `allow` / `deny`; `null` for a rule exemption.

status.description:
`"unresolved"`: the ref names nobody egret knows. `"empty"`: it names a
group that exists and has no members, so it matches nobody TODAY.

reason.description: Why it matches nobody, as a sentence an author can act on.

failsOpen.description:
Matching nobody here makes the compiled policy allow MORE than the model
states: an unresolved ref in a deny grant's include, an allow grant's
exclude, or a rule exemption's exclude. An allow include, a deny grant's
exclude (a `denyExceptions` item: naming nobody makes the deny wider)
and an exemption include matching nobody fail closed, and an `empty`
group never fails open: nobody is in it, so matching nobody is exactly
its meaning.

semantic_type.description: Semantic role driving smart rendering and chart defaults; "" = none. Rejected with 400 if not one of the listed values.

UpdateDashboard.description:
The dashboard PUT body — and, byte for byte, one stored revision (migration 0107).
`Serialize` is derived alongside `Deserialize` so the snapshot is produced from this exact
type rather than hand-built JSON that could drift from it; a compile error is how a new field
announces that revisions must carry it too.

UpdateEndpointInput.description:
The `PATCH` body: every field absent means "leave it alone".

`folder_id` and `source_ref` are nullable columns, so "absent" and "set to
null" are different requests and a plain `Option<Uuid>` cannot tell them
apart — an author moving an endpoint back to the root would silently get "no
change". They use [`double_option`], where absent is `None` and an explicit
`null` is `Some(None)`.

`state` and `live_version_id` are NOT here. They are the publish lifecycle,
and a draft edit must never be able to put an endpoint live or repoint what a
live one serves.
`deny_unknown_fields` for the same reason as [`CreateEndpointInput`]: on a
PATCH the failure mode is worse, because a typo'd key looks exactly like
"leave it alone" and the author sees the OLD value persist rather than a
zeroed one.

statements.description:
Replaces the whole list when present. There is no per-statement patch:
the order is part of the definition, so "edit statement 2" and "insert a
statement" would need an addressing scheme the list itself already is.

Bounded in the contract the same way `CreateEndpointInput` is, and for
the same reason: this route replaces the whole list, so it is the other
way a client can send one that is too long.

UpdateExternalEngine.description:
`PATCH /api/control-plane/engines/{id}/external`: every field optional;
an absent field is left as it is.

authzServiceId.description:
The policy profile to bind: absent leaves the binding, `null` unbinds,
a number binds (same rules as at registration).

host.description: New host (bare host: no scheme, port or path).

rangerPluginVersion.description:
The Ranger plugin version installed on the engine, as at registration.
The response says whether egret's evaluator models the (type, version)
pair.

UpdateFlowRequest.description:
`PUT /flows/{id}` body — a full replace, following the route's verb: the
whole draft (source, and therefore its derived namespace/flow_id/plan) is
replaced by what is sent, and `folder_id` is set to exactly what is sent
(including `None`, which clears it).

if_updated_at.description:
The draft's `updated_at` as the editor last read it (RFC 3339, the
exact string `FlowDto.updated_at` carried -- microseconds included).
When present and no longer the row's, the save is refused with 409
and nothing is written; absent, the save is unconditional. Publishing
also moves `updated_at`.

UpdateRegistryCatalogBody.description: Replaces config/advanced/description; name and kind never change.

UpdateSchedule.description:
Update body. Same shape as create minus `type`, which is immutable: an alert
and a report have disjoint required fields, so flipping the type of an
existing row can only produce a row that violates its own constraints.

dataapi_endpoint_id.description: `None` is workspace-scoped: watch every endpoint rather than one.

dataapi_error_code.description:
Required, and only meaningful, when `dataapi_metric` is
`error_code_count` — `schedule_dataapi_error_code_needs_metric` /
`schedule_dataapi_metric_needs_error_code` (migration 0128).

message.description:
A user-authored note carried into the notification body. Distinct from
`description`, which is the line the LIST shows.

message_footer.description:
The closing note, rendered UNDER the result — `message` opens the
notification, this one closes it, and an inline image sits between them.
Defaulted, so a client written before 0116 keeps working unchanged.

skip_if_empty.description: Metabase's `skip_if_empty`: send nothing when the run produced no rows.

targets.description:
Objects a REPORT delivers, in page order. Empty falls back to the
single `chart_id`/`dashboard_id`, which is every pre-0115 row.

UpdateSecretInput.description:
Request body for updating a global named secret. Any subset may be present:
a `name` triggers a rename (re-describing with `description`); a `type`+`data`
(or legacy `value`) rotates the underlying vault row.

UserRef.description: A minimal user reference (id + email) for the impersonation state on `/me`.

ValidateFlowRequest.description:
`POST /flows/{id}/validate` body — the UNSAVED source being checked. See
this module's doc comment for why this is a body field and not simply
"validate the stored draft".

ValidationReportDto.description:
A flow's validation report, over the wire. Errors block publish; warnings
do not — see [`ValidationReport`]'s own doc comment.

ValidatorType.description: How an alert's query result becomes a fire/don't-fire decision.

starrocksMaterializedViews.description: `null` when at least one listing failed; see `starrocks_list_error`.

starrocksListError.description:
Set exactly when `starrocks_materialized_views` is `null`; names each
failing engine.

enginesNotChecked.description:
Engines that reach the classification but were not asked (external, or
not running). Their views are unknown, not absent.

trinoViews.description:
The views in egret's catalogs that the DEFINER audit lists (spec B5):
their lineage reaches a table of this classification, or a table a mask
or row-filter rule selects, or is unknown. `null` when egret's catalogs
could not all be listed; see `trino_list_error`.

trinoListError.description:
Set exactly when `trino_views` is `null`; names what could not be
listed.

ViewExposureItem.description:
One view that reads a classified table. Shared by the StarRocks list and the
Trino list (filled by a later task).

catalog.description: Where the view lives: `default_catalog` for every StarRocks view.

owner.description: The DEFINER's `trino.run-as-owner`; `null` for any other mode.

ownerCleared.description:
Whether the owner is cleared for every classification the bases carry.
`null` when it cannot be said: not DEFINER, lineage not computed, or a
reached clearance names only groups. Read from current role membership.

bases.description: The recorded base tables, sorted; empty unless `computed`.

WarnedPolicy.description: One policy that carries at least one [`PolicyWarning`].

url_path.description:
`/workflows/v1/{workspace}/executions/webhook/{namespace}/{flow}/{key}`,
each segment percent-encoded, with the key rendered. A path, not a URL:
the server does not know the origin a caller reaches it on. `null` when
the key does not render.

unsupported.description: A declared option egret does not implement; a request is refused.

WhoCanAccess.description:
Reverse of `EffectiveAccess`: for one object, every principal who can reach it
and why (`who_can_access`). Mirror of the principal→access resolver.

oneOf.description:
See the module doc: `why` stays a `Vec`, never collapsed to one
cause.

WireDisagreement.description: Wire mirror of [`Disagreement`], plus its one-line rendering.

WireEngineType.description:
Wire mirror of [`EngineType`].

**`lowercase`, not `snake_case`, and that is the whole point (SP4d-2a
Task 5 review, I3).** `rename_all = "snake_case"` renders `StarRocks` as
`star_rocks`, and this API surface already publishes the other spelling:
`egret_query_api::Engine` is `rename_all = "lowercase"` and serialises
`starrocks`, which is also the literal stored in
`policy.authz_services.type` and matched by
`egret_perm_compile::trigger::engine_type_for`. A client correlating an
`ExplainProfile`'s `engine` with a profile's service type would otherwise
have to translate between two spellings of one word inside one document.
`lowercase` gives `trino` / `starrocks` and makes them the same string.

WirePluginVersion.description:
Wire mirror of [`PluginVersion`]. Renamed explicitly rather than through
`rename_all`: the source identifiers (`Ranger2_5_0`) already embed
digits and underscores, and `rename_all`'s case-boundary heuristic has no
good answer for that shape.

WireTagAttachmentProblem.description:
Wire mirror of [`TagAttachmentProblem`]: what one resolved tag ATTACHMENT
carries that the evaluator cannot reproduce (SP4d-2b Task 4).

Three `kind`s rather than one sentence, for the same reason
[`WireTagResourceProblem`] has four: the remedies differ and do not overlap.
`options` and `validity_periods` say the tag download carries a validity
construct egret neither emits nor evaluates; `resource_levels` says the
download's service resource is not a shape egret's own writer can produce at
all, which is a question about where the payload came from.

WireTagNormalisationProblem.description:
Wire mirror of [`TagNormalisationProblem`]: what a tag policy carries that
the TAG policy repository's `normalizeAndPrunePolicies` would rewrite or
reject (SP4d-2b Task 5).

Three `kind`s, and the third is not a variation on the first two: the two
namespaced arms are a WRONG ANSWER this crate declines to give, and
`mask_type_absent` is a CRASH — the plugin cannot build a policy engine from
that download, so nothing it serves is answered. A steward reading
"unsupported tag policy" would have no way to tell "rename the access type"
from "this download breaks the plugin outright", and the second is an
incident.

WireTagPolicyBlock.description:
Wire mirror of [`TagPolicyBlock`]. `Policies` carries its count as a
JSON number (`count`), never folded into a formatted string — Task 8's
steward UI renders it, and SP4d-2b changes what it means.

WireTagResourceProblem.description:
Wire mirror of [`TagResourceProblem`]: why a tag policy's resource map is
one the evaluator cannot filter the way Ranger's `RangerResourceTrie` does
(SP4d-2b Task 2).

Carried as its own `kind`, not a formatted string, for the same reason
[`WireTagPolicyBlock`] carries a `count`: a steward has to be able to tell
"this policy names a second resource level" from "this policy's tag value is
a wildcard", and the remedies differ.

oneOf.description:
`policy_ids`/`policy_names` are the FULL tied set — see
[`UndecidableCause::EvalOrderAmbiguous`]'s own doc for why collapsing
this to one id would misreport a tie this crate cannot order.

The `tagPolicies` block carries policies this decision's type would
evaluate and the caller resolved no tag set. Not reachable through
`explain` yet: the tag phase is not composed with the resource phase
until SP4d-2b Task 3.

A tag mask or row-filter policy that produced a result is also
deny-capable, so Ranger can report its id with a later policy's mask.

A tag policy the TAG policy repository would rewrite or remove on the way
in, in a way the evaluator does not reproduce — or, for
`mask_type_absent`, one that makes the plugin throw while building its
repository so that it serves nothing at all.

Two or more tag policies at DIFFERENT `policyPriority` each decide, and
the engine settles which survives with an arbitration the evaluator does
not model.

The three lists are POSITIONAL — `policy_ids[i]`, `policy_names[i]` and
`priorities[i]` describe one policy — for the same reason
[`WireUndecidableCause::EvalOrderAmbiguous`] carries two: a steward needs
to see which policies are in contention and at what priority, and
flattening that into a sentence would lose the priorities, which are the
thing to change.

A tag ALLOW in force and a **resource** policy at a strictly higher
priority that also allows — Ranger settles the composite through
`accessTypeResults`, which the evaluator does not reproduce.

# ⚠ Its own variant, because the alias put a wrong NOUN in front of a steward

The evaluator's `AccessPriorityCompositeNotModelled` first rode
[`WireUndecidableCause::TagPriorityArbitrationNotModelled`] as a documented
alias — same arbitration, same three positional lists, no new schema — so
that the Critical could land without racing the three files this split
needs. The cost was one word: that sentence opens "Several **tag** policies
…", and here one of the two is a RESOURCE policy. Names, ids, priorities and
the remedy were all correct; the noun was not, which is this branch's
recurring defect class (a label true of some of the states it is shown for).

So the two fields are NAMED rather than positional: the steward-facing fact
is *which* policy is the tag one, and a `Vec` cannot say that. Measured
rarity, for the copy's sake: **0 of 1148** composed-random cases and 10 of
4000 overall, so the sentence must not imply it is common.

tag_policy_id.description:
The tag policy whose ALLOW was in force. It can only be the tag
phase's: `allowed` becomes true at one site, which also sets
`priority`, and evaluation is priority-DESCENDING, so any later
candidate has `found.priority <= priority` — proved, not sampled.

resource_policy_id.description: The resource policy at a strictly higher priority that also allowed.

oneOf.description:
A tag DENY and a strictly higher-priority resource policy that allows —
a shape Ranger 2.5.0 and 2.8.0 answer DIFFERENTLY, so it can only be
decided once the running plugin version is known.

The plugin version the caller declared, or `null` if it declared none.

The two states need DIFFERENT advice and the UI branches on it: a known
2.5.0 means the running plugin is identified and the refusal is that
2.5.0's arm is unmodelled — there is nothing to record. `null` means the
caller did not say, and recording it would make half of these
answerable. `2_8_0` never appears: that is the version the evaluator
reproduces, so the refusal is not raised for it.

A tag mask or row filter was displaced in part by a strictly
higher-priority resource policy: Ranger reports the tag policy's id with
the resource policy's mask.

Whether Ranger's candidate filter (its resource trie) returns this policy
decides the request, and the evaluator cannot establish which way.

One tag ATTACHMENT in this request's resolved set carries something the
evaluator cannot reproduce. Named by TAG rather than by policy: the
construct is on the tag download, and it changes every tag policy's
candidacy at once.

WireUndecidableCause.description:
Wire mirror of [`UndecidableCause`]. `kind` is the discriminator a
frontend switches on; see the module doc for how the constructs each
cause names (`Unmodelled`, `ServiceDefIssue`) are mirrored just as
exhaustively, one level deeper.

WireUnmodelled.description:

listing's row ([`WorkflowNamespaceDto`]) and whether the caller may

flows.description: Flows in exactly this namespace that are not deleted.

files.description: Live namespace files (directories are not counted).

kv_keys.description: Live KV keys (the latest revision neither deleted nor expired).

own.description:

can_manage.description:
The caller holds `workflow:manage` in this workspace: the same PDP

WorkflowNamespaceDto.description:
One namespace of the workspace (W7d spec §3.1). egret has no namespace
table: a namespace exists while a flow that is not deleted, a live
namespace file or directory (even an empty one) or a live KV key is in
it, or while it is a parent by dots of one that is.

**The counts are this namespace's OWN**, never rolled up from its
children: `company` with one flow in `company.team` answers `flows: 0`.

`NamespaceDto` (the catalog's), and a second one of that name is dropped.

flows.description: Flows in exactly this namespace that are not deleted.

files.description:
Live namespace files (a path whose latest revision is not deleted;

kv_keys.description: Live KV keys (the latest revision neither deleted nor expired).

own.description:
False when the namespace is present only as a parent by dots of
another (its counts are then all zero). True for a source, whose
